author: Tony Hsieh
concept: A business also creates a way of life
quote: It wasn’t just about money. Together, we had built a business that combined profits, passion and purpose. And we knew that it wasn’t just about building a business. It was about building a lifestyle that was about delivering happiness to everyone, including ourselves.
refresher: A company shapes ordinary days for employees, customers, and its founders. Alongside financial results, consider what kind of relationships and daily experience its practices produce.

links.title: Self-Determination Theory · Autonomy, competence, and relatedness

author: Jay Samit
quote: A disruption in one link in the value chain creates opportunity in other links.
refresher: A change in one industry can create unmet needs for its suppliers, partners, or customers. Map the surrounding activities to see which new bottleneck or service becomes valuable after the change.

links.title: David J. Teece · Profiting from technological innovation and complementary assets (research paper)

author: Jonathan Safran Foer
quote: Cruelty is not only the willful causing of unnecessary suffering, but the indifference to it. It's much easier to be cruel than one might think. Nature isn't cruel. Cruelty depends on an understanding of cruelty, and the ability to choose against it. Or to choose to ignore it.
refresher: Foer extends the question of cruelty beyond deliberate harm to the choice not to notice it. Consider which consequences of ordinary consumption remain hidden by distance, convenience, or habit.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · The moral status of animals

author: Carolyn Elliott
concept: A feeling is not a moral verdict
quote: It just means you can let the feeling arise in your body, feel it without judging it, and stay centered and present with the flow of life instead of throwing yourself into a stinky pool of reactive guilt.
refresher: The passage invites noticing an uncomfortable feeling without turning it into guilt about your character. Acknowledging a feeling does not require endorsing it or acting on it.

links.title: Kristin Neff · Self-compassion (research review)

author: Ashlee Vance
quote: The more he thought about space, the more important its exploration seemed to him. He felt as if the public had lost some of its ambition and hope for the future.
refresher: In this biographical passage, space exploration stands for a society’s willingness to imagine a larger future. Consider which shared projects make possibility visible to people beyond their immediate participants.

links.title: Greater Good · The psychology of awe

book: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
author: Hunter S. Thompson
concept: A narrator can lose the thread
quote: Jesus! Did I say that? Or just think it? Was I talking? Did they hear me?
refresher: The speaker cannot tell whether a thought became speech. That instability is part of the reading experience: distinguish what a narrator reports from what the scene lets you confidently infer.

source.file: Fear and loathing in las vegas notes.html

links.title: Living Handbook of Narratology · Unreliable narration

author: Jessica Fern
quote: Relationship structure does not guarantee emotional security.
refresher: An agreed relationship structure says how a relationship is organized. Feeling secure also depends on lived experiences of responsiveness and reliability; the label alone cannot provide those experiences.

links.title: R. Chris Fraley · Attachment in adulthood (research review)

author: Chuck Palahniuk
quote: Then you're trapped in your lovely nest, and the things you used to own, now they own you.
refresher: The narrator’s possessions begin to dictate his life. Before acquiring something, consider the storage, maintenance, attention, and lifestyle it will require after the excitement of purchase has passed.

links.title: Greater Good · Why we think money buys happiness

author: Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner
concept: A fine can become a price
quote: After the fine was enacted, the number of late pickups promptly went… up.
refresher: In the daycare study discussed here, charging for lateness was followed by more late pickups. One interpretation is that payment replaced a social obligation with a purchasable service. The response to a penalty depends on how people understand it.

links.title: Gneezy and Rustichini · A Fine Is a Price (research paper, PDF)

author: Steven Tadelis
quote: When decisions need to be made over time, a rational player will solve his problem “backwards” so that early decisions take into account later decisions.
refresher: In a sequential decision, an early move changes later options. Start at the final choice, identify what would make sense there, and work backward to evaluate today’s move.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Game theory and sequential choices

book: Le crepe sono fatte per l’oro
author: Elena Giappone
concept: Meet a forest through the senses
quote: Shinrin-yoku è la pratica giapponese di immergersi nella natura non per fare esercizio fisico, ma per assorbire l'atmosfera del bosco attraverso tutti i sensi.
refresher: Shinrin-yoku means taking in the forest atmosphere. The emphasis is sensory contact: notice sounds, textures, light, and scent without turning the walk into a distance or speed target.

author: Seth Godin
quote: Write down under what circumstances are you willing to quit. And when. And then stick with it. If you decide in the now you'll probably talk yourself into quitting or make bad decision (e.g. when to quit a marathon, and you're tired while doing it)
refresher: Decide what evidence or circumstances would justify stopping before fatigue or frustration arrives. An advance stopping rule gives you a reference point when the immediate urge to quit becomes persuasive.

author: Daniel Goleman
quote: A failure to focus inward leaves you rudderless, a failure to focus on others renders you clueless, and a failure to focus outward may leave you blindsided.
refresher: Self-awareness, attention to other people, and attention to wider systems answer different questions. When a decision feels incomplete, check which of these three directions you have neglected.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Attention and selection

author: Jonathan Haidt
quote: Risk of minor injuries should be a feature, not a bug, in playground design.
refresher: Haidt argues that eliminating every chance of a minor mishap changes what play can teach. A useful distinction is a challenge a child can assess versus a hidden danger they cannot reasonably recognize.

links.title: Canadian Paediatric Society · Outdoor risky play

book: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow
author: Aurélien Géron
quote: Overfitting the training data: the model performs well on the training data but it does not generalize well.
refresher: A model may learn accidental details of its training examples and fail on new ones. Keep evaluation data separate from fitting and tuning so a strong score reflects generalization rather than familiarity.

author: Yuval Noah Harari
concept: Performance and experience are different questions
quote: Science knows surprisingly little about mind and consciousness. They don’t know how a collection of electric brain signals creates subjective experiences.
refresher: Explaining how a system processes information does not by itself explain why there is something it feels like to be that system. Separate observable capability from claims about subjective experience.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Consciousness and subjective experience

author: Isaac Asimov
quote: Rule Three drives him back and Rule Two drives him forward, so he follows a circle around the selenium pool, staying on the locus of all points of potential equilibrium.
refresher: In Asimov’s fictional robot, competing directives produce a loop rather than a useful action. When specifying rules, examine their interactions and priorities in edge cases, not just each rule in isolation.

links.title: NASA · Checking software requirements for consistency

book: Journey to the Centre of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
quote: However great and mighty the marvels of nature may seem to us, they are always to be explained by physical reasons. Everything is subordinate to some great law of nature.
refresher: The novel’s confidence in natural explanation is distinct from the accuracy of its imagined geology. A remarkable observation can start an investigation: what mechanism might produce it, and how could that account be examined?

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Scientific method and explanation

author: Haruki Murakami
quote: That’s why I listen to Schubert while I’m driving. All the performances are imperfect. A dense, artistic kind of imperfection stimulates your consciousness, keeps you alert.
refresher: The speaker values performances whose unresolved qualities continue to engage the listener. Artistic interest need not come from flawless execution; it can arise from tension that leaves something to interpret.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Attention and selection

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
quote: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM): If the ratio of users (or any randomization unit) between the variants is not close to the designed ratio, the experiment suffers from a Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM). It likely indicate a problem that requires debugging.
refresher: Before interpreting an A/B test, check whether the observed allocation is statistically compatible with the intended split. A meaningful mismatch can signal assignment, logging, or filtering problems that undermine the comparison.

book: Exploring the World of Lucid Dreaming
author: Stephen LaBerge and Howard Rheingold
quote: One way to become lucid is to ask yourself whether or not you are dreaming while you are dreaming. In order to do this, you should make a habit of asking the question while awake.
refresher: Lucidity means recognizing that you are dreaming while the dream continues. The book proposes questioning your state as a practice; awareness of dreaming and control over the dream are separate abilities.

author: Rand Fishkin
quote: Every email should be written and every conversation conducted as though it will one day be leaked.
refresher: Private messages can travel beyond their original audience. Before sending one, consider whether its claims, tone, and treatment of others would remain defensible if the context became public.

links.title: Markkula Center for Applied Ethics · Test a decision before a public audience

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: A baseline is essential to make sure that the model works better than a simple heuristics.
refresher: A complicated model needs a comparison point. Measure a basic heuristic or constant predictor on the same evaluation data; without that baseline, an impressive-looking score may represent little practical improvement.

links.title: scikit-learn · Dummy estimators as prediction baselines

author: Osvaldo Martin
quote: For a continuous random variable, we can only assign a probability of 0 to every individual value it may take; instead, we can assign densities to them and then we can calculate probabilities for a range of values.
refresher: For a continuous distribution with a density, the probability of an interval is the area under its density curve. The height at one value is a density, so it need not stay below one.

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Revenue growth can conceal weak economics
quote: So why are entrepreneurs programmed to pursue bigger and bigger and bigger? Because of an assumption that at a certain point all that revenue will yield a profit.
refresher: A growing top line does not establish that a business earns a profit or has cash available. Examine the expenses and cash flows accompanying growth instead of assuming that more sales will eventually solve everything.

links.title: SEC · A beginners’ guide to financial statements

author: Gabriel García Márquez
quote: The most fearsome part of the sickness of insomnia was not the impossibility of sleeping, for the body did not feel any fatigue at all, but its inexorable evolution toward a more critical manifestation: a loss of memory.
refresher: The novel’s insomnia plague becomes frightening through the loss of memory. Remembering is more than storing private experiences: it helps people maintain names, relationships, and the continuity of a community.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Memory and its relation to the past

author: Malcolm Gladwell
quote: Our arbitrary choice of cutoff dates is causing long-lasting effects, and no one care about them.
refresher: An arbitrary age cutoff can give some children an early advantage in selection and coaching. Later achievement may partly reflect those accumulated opportunities, not simply the ability visible at the finish.

links.title: Baker and colleagues · Nurturing sport expertise, including relative age effects (review paper, PDF)

author: Christopher M. Bishop
quote: Curse of dimensionality: the problem with an exponentially large number of cells is that we would need an exponentially large quantity of training data in order to ensure that the cells are not empty.
refresher: Adding features expands the space that data must cover. Even a large dataset can become sparse in many dimensions, making local comparisons and reliable estimation harder.

author: Patrick Süskind
quote: Perfume lives in time; it has its youth, its maturity, and its old age. And only if it gives off a scent equally pleasant at all three different stages of its life, can it be called successful.
refresher: The passage treats perfume as a sequence rather than a single impression. Its opening, middle, and lingering traces can differ, so evaluating it at one instant misses part of the composition.

links.title: Rob Brown · How a perfume changes from opening to dry-down

author: Thomas Piketty
quote: Inflation has the effect of redistributing wealth among asset categories rather than a long-term structural effect.
refresher: A rise in prices changes the purchasing power of nominal claims. Its effects differ across borrowers, savers, wages, and assets; an average inflation number does not describe every household’s experience.

author: Ray Dalio
quote: Reflect and write down decision-making criteria in form of algorithms whenever you make a decision.
refresher: Record which conditions led to a choice while the reasoning is fresh. On the next similar decision, you can examine and revise the rule rather than reconstructing an explanation from memory.

links.title: Michael Nygard · Recording a decision’s context and consequences

author: Brad J. Schoenfeld and Ronald L. Snarr
quote: The sliding filament theory states that a muscle shortens or lengthens when the filaments (actin and myosin) slide past each other, without the filaments themselves changing in length.
refresher: During a shortening contraction, actin and myosin overlap more as sarcomeres shorten. The filaments themselves do not need to shrink; their relative movement changes the length of the muscle’s working units.

author: Richard C. Schwartz
concept: Ask what an impulse is protecting
quote: In IFS, when parts do take over, we don’t shame them. Instead, we get curious and use the part’s impulse as a trailhead to find what is driving it that needs to be healed.
refresher: Internal Family Systems treats an impulse as a possible clue to a protective role. Within that framework, curiosity about its purpose replaces immediate self-condemnation; the metaphor need not be taken as a literal account of separate personalities.

author: Walter Isaacson
quote: I want it to be as beautiful as possible, even if it's inside the box. A great carpenter isn't going to use lousy wood for the back of a cabinet, even though nobody's going to see it.
refresher: The back of a cabinet matters to the craftsperson even when a customer will not inspect it. In software or other work, hidden structure affects how well the visible result can be maintained and improved.

author: J. E. Gordon
quote: Stress is a measure of how hard the atoms and molecules which make up the material are being pushed together or pulled apart as a result of the external forces. Stress = load / area
refresher: The same force can produce very different material stress depending on the area carrying it. A broad support and a narrow contact point are mechanically different even when the total load is identical.

author: Lao Tzu
quote: Those who do not trust enough will not be trusted.
refresher: This line suggests a reciprocal relationship between extending trust and receiving it. Consider how constant suspicion changes another person’s freedom to act and willingness to cooperate, while retaining appropriate boundaries.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Trust and distrust

author: Timothy Ferriss
concept: Look for an uneven distribution of results
quote: 80% of the outputs result from 20% of the inputs.
refresher: The 80/20 principle is a heuristic, not a universal ratio. Measure which activities or causes account for most of a result, then focus effort on the few that contribute disproportionately.

links.title: ASQ · Pareto analysis and the vital few

author: Paulo Coelho
concept: Wonder and duty can share attention
quote: The secret of happiness is to see all the marvels of the world, and never to forget the drops of oil on the spoon.
refresher: The spoon image holds two tasks together: attending to the world’s beauty and caring for what has been entrusted to you. The story invites a balance between exploration and responsibility.

links.title: Ronnie McBryer · Balancing wonder and responsibility (commentary)

author: Sun Tzu
quote: Treat prisoners of war kindly
refresher: This brief instruction concerns the treatment of captives. A person’s defeat does not erase their humanity; conduct toward someone under your power is a separate question from whether you prevailed.

links.title: ICRC · Humane treatment and dignity in detention

author: Olivia Fox Cabane
concept: Capability and goodwill send different signals
quote: Power means being perceived as able to affect the world around us. Warmth is goodwill towards others.
refresher: Others may judge both whether you can act effectively and whether your intentions are friendly. Competence without goodwill can feel threatening; warmth without apparent capability can fail to inspire confidence.

links.title: Fiske, Cuddy, and Glick · Warmth and competence (research paper)

author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
concept: The symbol can outgrow its object
quote: It had occurred to him that the colossal significance of that light had now vanished forever. Now it was again a green light on a dock. His count of enchanted objects had diminished by one.
refresher: Gatsby’s green light carries an imagined future far larger than a lamp across the water. When the object becomes attainable, its symbolic power changes. Notice when longing adds qualities the object itself cannot supply.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Desire and attachment

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: An hyperparameter is a property of a learning algorithm that influences the way the algorithm works. Those values aren’t learned by the algorithm itself from data. They have to be set by the data analyst before running the algorithm.
refresher: A hyperparameter configures how learning happens, rather than being a fitted model value. Choosing it using validation results is still part of model development, so final test data must remain separate.

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: A growing industry is not enough
quote: Obvious prospects for physical growth in a business do not translate into obvious profits for investors.
refresher: An industry can expand while investors receive disappointing returns. The price paid, competition, costs, and who captures the gains all matter; a compelling growth story alone does not establish an attractive investment.

links.title: SEC · Financial statements, earnings, and valuation ratios

author: Douglas Murray
concept: Dignity is not conditional on control
quote: One of the most significant building blocks of contemporary morality: the fundamental recognition that it is wrong to punish, demean or look down to people for characteristics over which they have no control.
refresher: The passage identifies a reason to reject humiliation based on unchosen characteristics. Respect for people also need not depend on proving why a trait exists; evaluate actions without treating identity as a moral fault.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Respect and moral standing

author: Culadasa (John Yates), Matthew Immergut, and Jeremy Graves
quote: The scope of attention is how wide or narrow you want your focus to be.
refresher: Attention has a width as well as a target. Noticing a single sensation and taking in the whole soundscape are different tasks; deliberately widening or narrowing the field changes what becomes prominent.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Attention and selection

book: The Old Man and the Sea
author: Ernest Hemingway
concept: Act with the materials at hand
quote: You should have brought many things, he thought. But you did not bring them, old man. Now is no time to think of what you do not have. Think of what you can do with what there is.
refresher: The fisherman interrupts regret about missing equipment to consider what remains possible. Preparation has its moment; once a situation is underway, inventorying available means can restore a useful next step.

author: Joseph Campbell with Bill Moyers
quote: Society has provided young people no rituals by which they become members of the tribe, of the community.
refresher: Campbell worries about the absence of recognized transitions into community life. A shared ceremony can make a change of role visible, giving both the newcomer and the group a way to acknowledge it.

links.title: Greater Good · How classroom rituals create community

author: Eckhart Tolle
quote: "Large-scale waiting" is waiting for the next vacation, for a better job, for the children to grow up, for a truly meaningful relationship, for success, to make money, to be important, to become enlightened. Is not uncommon for people to spend their whole life waiting to start living. Waiting is a state of mind.
refresher: Waiting for a promotion, holiday, or relationship can turn the present into a holding area. Identify one worthwhile part of living that need not remain conditional on the next milestone.

links.title: Arthur C. Brooks · How to set the right life goals and avoid the arrival fallacy

author: Brad Stone
quote: Airbnb can be considered the biggest hotel company on the planet, yet it possesses no actual hotel rooms. Uber is among the world’s largest car serviced, yet it doesn’t employ any professional drivers or own any vehicles.
refresher: The passage describes the platform model at the time of the book: coordinating transactions without owning the underlying rooms or vehicles. It shifts attention from producing each asset to organizing access, trust, and participation.

links.title: Jean Tirole · Two-sided platforms and market regulation (Nobel lecture slides, PDF)

author: Naomi Klein
quote: Pushing global temperatures past certain thresholds could trigger abrupt, unpredictable and potentially irreversible changes that have massively disruptive and large-scale impacts. At that point, eve if we do not add any additional CO2 to the atmosphere, potentially unstoppable processes are set in motion.
refresher: Some Earth-system changes can persist after the original pressure stops increasing. That makes the path and peak of warming important, alongside eventual stabilization; crossing a threshold may close off an easy return.

author: Harper Lee
quote: Thus the dicta No Crawford Minds His Own Business, Every Third Merriweather Is Morbid, The Truth Is Not in the Delafields, All the Bufords Walk Like That.
refresher: The town’s inherited sayings turn families into supposedly predictable types. Such labels can replace attention to an individual’s conduct. Ask whether a judgment rests on something observed or on a story attached to a group.

book: The Existential Importance of the Penis
author: Daniel N. Watter
quote: Existential isolation implies the most basic of all forms of isolation, the awareness that no matter how close or connected we may be to others, there is an ""unbridgeable gulf" between us and any other human being.
refresher: In Yalom’s framework, discussed by Watter, existential isolation concerns the separateness of each person’s experience, even within close relationships. It differs from lacking company; connection does not require another person to experience life exactly as you do.

author: Joe Dispenza
quote: The nocebo is the opposite of the placebo (Latin for "I shall harm", as opposed of "I shall please" of placebo).
refresher: Nocebo effects concern adverse experiences influenced by negative expectations and context. The concept does not mean that illness is imagined or that belief can replace treatment; it distinguishes one influence on experience from the condition’s other causes.

author: Timothy Ferriss
quote: Disagree and commit in meetings (pag. 172)
refresher: Your note flags a way to move forward without pretending everyone agrees. State the disagreement, let the responsible person decide, then support the agreed course in good faith. Commitment concerns execution, not a requirement to change your belief.

author: Timothy Ferriss
quote: Double or triple threat (pag. 269)
refresher: Your reminder points to a career advantage built from a useful combination. Writing, technical knowledge, and presentation may reinforce one another even when none is exceptional alone. Ask which additional skill would make your existing strengths more useful together.

links.title: Josh Kaufman · Combining complementary skills

author: Timothy Ferriss
quote: Try poverty (pag. 475)
refresher: Your note points to the Stoic exercise of briefly choosing fewer comforts to examine what you actually need. Ferriss discusses it through Seneca. A modest experiment, such as an ordinary meal instead of a luxury purchase, can test an imagined dependence; chosen simplicity is not the same as involuntary poverty.

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: Duplication can reveal a missing abstraction
quote: Clean code contains no duplication. When the same thing is done over and over, it's a sign that there is an idea in our mind that is not well represented in the code.
refresher: When the same rule appears in several places, changing it requires coordinated edits. Look for the shared idea behind the repetition. Similar-looking code that changes for different reasons may still belong apart.

links.title: Martin Fowler · Kent Beck’s rules of simple design

author: Robert C. Martin
quote: Side effects are lies. Your function promises to do one thing, but it also does other hidden things.
refresher: A function that appears to inspect something should not secretly modify it. Separating observations from state changes makes calls easier to compose and reason about; when a combined operation is useful, make its behavior clear.

links.title: Martin Fowler · Command-query separation

author: Steven Tadelis
quote: Any strategy profile for which players are playing mutual best responses is a Nash equilibrium, making this equilibrium concept self-enforcing.
refresher: At a Nash equilibrium, no player can improve their payoff by changing only their own strategy while the others hold theirs fixed. Stability in this sense does not mean the outcome is fair or best for the group.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Equilibrium and dominance in games

author: Steven Tadelis
quote: Rational players will never play a dominated strategy and will always play a dominant strategy when it exists.
refresher: A strictly dominated strategy does worse than another strategy for every possible choice by the other players. Eliminating it requires comparing across all those possibilities, rather than rejecting it because it loses in just one scenario.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Equilibrium and dominance in games

author: Aurélien Géron
concept: More data cannot repair every sampling bias
quote: Nonrepresentative training data (e.g. sample is too small -> sampling noise, sampling method is flawed -> sampling bias)

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Accuracy can hide a neglected class
quote: Class imbalance can significantly affect the performance of the model. Techniques as over- and undersampling can help to overcome the problem.

author: Osvaldo Martin
quote: Probabilities are used to measure the uncertainty we have about parameters, and Bayes' theorem is a mechanism to correctly update those probabilities in light of new data, hopefully reducing our uncertainty.
refresher: Bayesian inference combines a prior with how likely the observed data would be under each candidate explanation. The result is a posterior distribution. New evidence changes degrees of uncertainty rather than automatically proving a single explanation.

quote: As a third reason, the Beta distribution is the conjugate prior to the Binomial distribution. A conjugate prior of a likelihood is a prior that, when used in combination with a given likelihood, returns a posterior with the same functional form as the prior.
refresher: A conjugate prior and likelihood produce a posterior in the prior’s distribution family. For a binomial model with a beta prior, observations update the beta parameters. This makes calculation convenient without guaranteeing that the model fits reality.

quote: Statistical power is the probability of detecting a meaningful difference between the variants when there really is one (statistically, reject the null wher there is a difference).

quote: Proximity: We tend to think of objects that are physically close together as belonging to part of a group.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
quote: The principle of social proof states that one means we use to determine what is correct is to find out what other people think is correct.
refresher: When uncertain, people often use others’ behavior as evidence of what to do. Before following a crowd, ask whether its members have independent information or are simply copying one another.

links.title: Nielsen Norman Group · Social proof in user experience

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: A drop in availability can raise desire
quote: What really matter is also the differential value of availability: the drop from abundance to scarcity of something produced a decidedly more positive reaction than did constant scarcity.
refresher: An item becoming scarce may feel more desirable than an item that was always scarce. Notice whether urgency comes from the item’s usefulness or from a recent loss of availability; those are different reasons to value it.

links.title: Worchel, Lee, and Adewole · Scarcity and judgments of value (research paper)

author: Rob Fitzpatrick
concept: A customer description needs a meeting place
quote: Rule of thumb: Good customer segments are a who-where pair. If you don't know where to go to find your customers, keep slicing your segment into smaller pieces until you do.
refresher: A segment becomes actionable when you can name both the people and where to reach them. A professional community, event, or specific workplace gives an interview plan a practical starting point.

links.title: Paul Graham · Finding and recruiting early users

author: Rob Fitzpatrick
quote: Commitment - They are showing they’re serious by giving up something they value such as time. reputation, or money
refresher: Time spent on a pilot, an introduction that risks reputation, or a payment shows a different level of involvement from verbal enthusiasm. Ask what concrete next step someone is willing to take, without treating every kind of commitment as equivalent.

links.title: Effectuation · Partnerships built through commitments

book: Structures: Or Why Things Don’t Fall Down
author: J. E. Gordon
quote: Strain tells us how far two points in a solid are being pulled apart. Strain = amount stretched / length.
refresher: A millimeter of stretch means something different in a short wire and a long cable. Strain divides the change in length by the original length, allowing deformation to be compared across different sizes.

links.title: OpenStax · Strain and elastic deformation

author: Chris Voss with Tahl Raz
concept: Invite the other side to solve the obstacle
quote: Ask for help or an advice. That gives the other part the illusion of control and make him use his mental and emotional resources to overcome your challenges.
refresher: An open question about how an agreement could work can reveal constraints and alternatives that a demand would miss. Ask for the other person’s reasoning while stating your own limits honestly.

links.title: Harvard Program on Negotiation · Asking better negotiation questions

author: Arthur C. Clarke
quote: Turing had pointed out that, if one could carry out a prolonged conversation with a machine without being able to distinguish between its replies and those that a man might give, then the machine was thinking, by any sensible definition of the word.
refresher: Clarke’s passage invokes Turing’s conversational test. The test shifts attention to what an evaluator can distinguish through dialogue; whether successful imitation establishes thinking or consciousness remains a separate philosophical question.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · The Turing test and its limits

author: Osvaldo Martin
concept: Expected value is a weighted average
quote: If X is a discrete random variable, we can compute its expected value as: E(X)= sum over x of x*P(X=x)
refresher: Multiply each possible outcome by its probability and add the results. This describes an average across the distribution, not the outcome you must receive in one attempt. Variability and the consequences of losses still matter.

author: Christopher M. Bishop
quote: The entropy is the lower bound on the number of bits needed to transmit the state of a random variable.
refresher: Shannon entropy measures average uncertainty in a source. With base-two logarithms, it gives an ideal lower bound on average bits per symbol for lossless coding under the model, not a measure of the message’s meaning.

author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
quote: ‘And I like large parties. They’re so intimate. At small parties there isn’t any privacy.'
refresher: The remark reverses the usual association between small gatherings and intimacy. A large party may let someone choose whom to engage with and escape constant notice; privacy depends partly on how attention is distributed.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Privacy and access to the person

author: Arthur C. Clarke
quote: One does not replace a blown fuse - until one knows just why it has blown.
refresher: A failed component may be a symptom rather than the cause. Before replacing it, identify what overloaded or damaged it so the same failure does not immediately return.

links.title: Google SRE · Learning from incidents through blameless postmortems

book: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
author: Burton G. Malkiel
quote: Systematic risk arises from the basic variability of stock prices in general and the tendency for all stock to go along with the general market (market risk), unsystematic risk results from factors peculiar to that particular company.
refresher: Company-specific risks can offset one another inside a diversified portfolio. Market-wide movements affect many holdings together, so some risk remains even after diversification.

book: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
author: Burton G. Malkiel
quote: Just to stay even, your investments have to produce a rate of return equal to inflation.
refresher: A nominal gain can still reduce purchasing power. Judge an investment’s result after accounting for the change in what money can buy.

book: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
quote: Because it expands, ice floats on water. It lacked this, ice would sink, and lakes and oceans would freeze from the bottom up. This are hardly the conditions to nurture life.
refresher: Water expands as it freezes, making solid ice less dense than liquid water. A floating surface layer insulates the water below instead of letting a lake freeze upward from its bed.

book: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
concept: Human life depends on microbial partners
quote: Bacteria will be here when the Sun explodes. This is their planet, and we are here only because they allow us to be. They got along for billions of years without us. We couldn’t survive a day without them.
refresher: Bacteria are ancient, resilient, and woven into the systems that sustain us. Thinking of the body as an isolated organism misses the work performed by its microbial communities.

author: Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
concept: A difficult fake exposes a difficult abstraction
quote: Building fakes for your abstractions is an excellent way to get design feedback: if it’s hard to fake, the abstraction is probably too complicated.
refresher: A test fake must reproduce an abstraction’s useful behavior simply. If the fake becomes elaborate, the production boundary may be doing too much or exposing the wrong interface.

author: James Clear
quote: The greatest threat to success is boredom. As soon as we experience the slightest dip in motivation, we begin seeking a new strategy. You have to fall in love with boredom.
refresher: Once novelty disappears, switching methods can feel more rewarding than continuing. Progress often depends on staying engaged with ordinary repetitions long enough to refine them.

author: John Carreyrou
concept: A culture that punishes doubt loses warnings
quote: The biggest problem of the device was the dysfunctional corporate culture in which it was being developed. Elizabeth and Sunny regarded anyone who raised a concern or an objection as a cynic and a naysayer.
refresher: Treating every objection as disloyalty filters out the information leaders most need. People must be able to raise concerns without being cast as enemies of the mission.

links.title: Center for Creative Leadership · Psychological safety research (PDF)

author: John Carreyrou
concept: Give the subject a fair chance to respond
quote: At the Journal, we had a cardinal rule called "No surprises." We never went to press with a story without informing the story subject of every piece of information we had gathered in our reporting and giving them ample time and opportunity to address and rebut everything.
refresher: Before publishing an allegation, show the subject the substance of what you intend to report and allow time for a meaningful response. The reply may correct an error or become part of the story.

links.title: Society of Professional Journalists · Code of Ethics

author: Osvaldo Martin
concept: Heavy tails make estimates more robust
quote: The Student’s t-distribution allows us to have a more robust estimation of the mean and standard deviation because the outliers have the effect of decreasing 𝜈 instead of pulling the mean or increasing the standard deviation.
refresher: A Student’s t model can accommodate extreme observations through its tail parameter. That keeps one outlier from dragging the estimated center and spread as strongly as it would under a normal model.

author: Osvaldo Martin
concept: Polynomial regression is linear in its coefficients
quote: There are two important things to notice. First, polynomial regression is still linear regression; the linearity refers to the coefficients (the fs), not the variables (the xs). The second thing to note is that we are creating new variables out of thin air.
refresher: A model can curve with respect to its input and still be a linear model. The label refers to how the unknown coefficients enter the equation, not to the shape drawn against the predictor.

author: Atul Gawande
concept: Memory weights the peak and the ending
quote: The ratings in term of pain in an clinical operation follow the "Peak-End rule", instead of the sum moment-by-moment, that is an average of the pain experienced at the single worst moment of the procedure and the very end.
refresher: People do not remember an experience as a simple sum of every moment. Its most intense point and its ending can disproportionately shape the retrospective judgment.

links.title: Kahneman and colleagues · When more pain is preferred to less (research paper)

book: Brief Answers to the Big Questions
author: Stephen Hawking
concept: Control matters more as capability grows
quote: Whereas the short-term impact of AI depends on who controls it, the long-term impact depends on whether it can be controlled at all. AI would be either the best or the worst thing ever happened to humanity. We should plan ahead.
refresher: Near-term effects depend on who directs a system; longer-term effects also depend on whether its behavior remains governable. Capability work therefore needs explicit goals, oversight, and failure planning.

author: Thomas Piketty
concept: Slow growth can raise capital’s relative weight
quote: The long term capital/income ratio is the savings rate divided by the growth rate. US has higher growth rate than Europe, that's why it has lower capital/income ratio.
refresher: In the simple long-run relationship described here, the capital-to-income ratio rises with saving and falls with economic growth. The same saving rate therefore accumulates more capital relative to income in a slower-growing economy.

author: James Gleick
concept: Iteration turns a formula into a process
quote: Standard geometry takes an equation and asks for the set of numbers that satisfy it. But when a geometer iterates an equation instead of solving it, the equation becomes a process instead of a description, dynamic instead of static.
refresher: Solving an equation asks which values satisfy it. Iterating one feeds each output back as the next input, revealing trajectories, attractors, and behavior over time.

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: Wrap third-party interfaces you do not control
quote: Wrapping third-party API is a best practice so you minimize your dependencies upon it, make it easier to mock it out for tests, and aren't tied to a particular vendor's API design choices.
refresher: A local boundary limits how much vendor-specific design leaks into the application. It also gives tests a stable seam and makes replacement less disruptive.

author: Robert C. Martin
quote: Having dirty tests is equivalent to, if not worse than, having no tests. Tests must change as the production code evolves. The dirtier the tests, the harder they are to change.
refresher: Tests change alongside production behavior. If they are hard to understand or modify, they slow safe changes and eventually stop providing trustworthy feedback.

links.title: Google Testing Blog · Test behavior, not implementation

author: John Arundel and Justin Domingus
quote: Distributed systems expose the limitations of traditional monitoring, because they're not in either up or down states: they exist in a constant state of partially degraded service. In other words, nothing is ever completely right aboard a ship.
refresher: A distributed system may keep serving some users while particular paths fail or slow down. Monitoring must describe partial health rather than forcing the whole service into a simple up-or-down label.

links.title: Google SRE · Monitoring distributed systems

author: John Arundel and Justin Domingus
concept: Grant only the permissions a workload needs
quote: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) gives you fine-grained management of permissions in Kubernetes. Make sure it's enabled, and use RBAC roles to grant specific users and apps only the minimum privileges they need to do their jobs.
refresher: Broad permissions enlarge the damage a mistake or compromise can cause. Define roles around specific duties and review exceptions rather than granting convenient blanket access.

source.file: Cloud native devops with kubernetes notes.html

links.title: Kubernetes documentation · RBAC good practices

author: Gianluca Gotto
concept: A familiar social circle can narrow possibility
quote: Fare conoscenza non sembra niente di troppo complesso, sulla carta. Ma solo quando ti trovi in una situazione come la mia ti rendi conto di quanto sia incredibile l'effetto di anni e anni trascorsi a frequentare sempre le stesse persone.
refresher: Years spent with the same people can make one social world feel like the whole world. Entering a new setting can reveal different norms, identities, and ways of relating.

author: Cal Newport
concept: Choose tools by their effect on what matters
quote: The Craftsman Approach to Tool Selection: Identify the core factors that determine success and happiness in your professional and personal life. Adopt a tool only if its positive impacts on these factors substantially outweigh its negative impacts.
refresher: A tool’s benefits are not enough on their own. Name the few factors that drive success and well-being, then weigh the tool’s positive and negative effects on those factors.

links.title: Center for Humane Technology · How persuasive technology captures attention

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Culture becomes part of the brand
quote: What’s the best way to build a brand for the long term? In a word: culture. If you get the culture right, most of other stuff will happen naturally on its own. Your culture is your brand.
refresher: Customers encounter a company through countless employee decisions. Shared norms shape those decisions, so the internal culture eventually appears in the external experience.

links.title: MIT Sloan Management Review · What strong corporate cultures get right

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: A promise must shape the whole operation
quote: Working in a call centre just wasn’t something that people in Bay Area wanted to do, but to build Zappos brand into being about the very best customer service, we needed to make sure customer service was the entire company.
refresher: If service defines the brand, the service team cannot be treated as a peripheral cost center. Hiring, training, authority, and operations all have to support the promise made to customers.

links.title: Harvard Business Review · The service-profit chain

author: Jay Samit
concept: Try to kill an idea before the market does
quote: An important step is to kill your idea. Find a problem that will derail your idea, because that is what the marketplace will do, and really well.
refresher: Before investing heavily, search deliberately for the assumption or failure mode that would make the idea collapse. Early disconfirmation is cheaper and more useful than late surprise.

links.title: Harvard Business Review · Performing a project premortem

author: Ashlee Vance
concept: Connected businesses can reinforce one another
quote: The unified filed theory of Elon Musk. Each one of his businesses is interconnected in the short term and the long term. Tesla makes better battery packs that SolarCity can then sell to end customers. SolarCity supplies Tesla's charging stations with solar panels, helping Tesla to provide free recharging to its drivers.
refresher: A portfolio becomes more than a list of companies when capabilities or infrastructure from one strengthen another. Map the exchanges explicitly; a claimed synergy matters only when something useful actually flows between them.

links.title: Harvard Business Review · Strategy in the ecosystem economy

book: Exploring the World of Lucid Dreaming
author: Stephen LaBerge and Howard Rheingold
concept: Dream recall depends on when you wake
quote: Dreams are not recalled unless the sleeper awakens directly from them. Try setting an alarm clock to awaken you at a time when you are likely to be dreaming. Multiple of ninety minutes from your bedtime.
refresher: Dream memories fade quickly unless waking interrupts or closely follows the dream. Timing an awakening near a likely REM period can create a better opportunity to record one.

author: Daniel Goleman
concept: Creative work alternates focus and release
quote: First we prepare our minds by gathering a wide variety of pertinent information and then we alternate between concentrating intently on the problem and letting our minds wander freely.
refresher: Preparation loads the mind with relevant material. Intense attention develops the problem; a looser period then allows remote associations to surface before another focused pass evaluates them.

author: Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner
concept: Conventional wisdom is a starting hypothesis
quote: The conventional wisdom in Galbraith’s view must be simple, convenient, comfortable, and comforting - though not necessarily true. It would be silly to argue that the conventional wisdom is never true, but noticing where it might be false is a nice place to start asking questions.
refresher: A familiar explanation may be true, but comfort and repetition are not evidence. Ask what observation would distinguish it from plausible alternatives.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Scientific method

author: Steven Tadelis
quote: Repeated games are useful frameworks to understand how people cooperate over time, how firms manage to collude in markets, and how reputations for good behaviour are sustained over time even when short-run temptations are present.
refresher: In a repeated relationship, today’s defection can change how others behave tomorrow. That shadow of the future can make cooperation rational even when a one-shot temptation points elsewhere.

links.title: Nobel Prize · Conflict and cooperation through game theory

author: Aurélien Géron
concept: Soft margins trade purity for robustness
quote: Strictly imposing that all instances must be off the street (hard margin classification) works only if data is separable and it's sensitive to outliers. Better allowing some margin violations, while limiting them (soft margin classification).
refresher: A hard-margin classifier requires perfect separation and can be dominated by an outlier. Allowing controlled violations produces a boundary that can generalize better to imperfect data.

author: Yuval Noah Harari
quote: Egyptians believed that only prayers to the living-god pharaoh could save Nile Valley from devastating floods and droughts. They were right. Pharaoh did nothing to raise or lower the Nile water level, but built dams and dug canals.
refresher: The pharaoh did not control the river, but the institution around him organized canals and dams. A mistaken causal story can still coordinate actions that produce real effects.

concept: Zero correlation does not mean no relationship
quote: When you’re told that two phenomena in nature or society were found to be uncorrelated, it doesn’t mean there’s no relationship, only that there’s no relationship of the sort that correlation is designed to detect.
refresher: Correlation measures a particular kind of association, usually linear dependence. A strong curved or otherwise structured relationship can still produce a coefficient near zero.

author: Isaac Asimov
concept: Passing a one-way test proves little

refresher: If robots obey three rules, breaking one would disprove robothood. Obeying them cannot confirm it because a human might behave the same way. Necessary evidence is not automatically sufficient evidence.

book: Le crepe sono fatte per l’oro
author: Elena Giappone
concept: Finish the present task before leaving it
quote: Nella vita, zanshin è l'arte di chiudere bene le cose. Non lasciare tutto a metà. Non correre già alla prossima cosa mentre stai ancora facendo questa. Rimanere presente fino alla fine. E anche un momento dopo la fine.

quote: Transparency is making the choice to reveal even the most uncomfortable truths with relentless candor. It is immensely powerful, and it has an almost unbelievably positive impact on everyone around you. You need to balance it with empathy.

concept: Training data should resemble production inputs
quote: It is important that the distribution of feature values in the training set is similar to the distribution of values the production model will receive. Furthermore, good features are unitary, easy to understand and maintain.

author: Viktor E. Frankl
concept: A life also accumulates irreversible value
quote: There is no reason to pity old people. Instead, young people should envy them. They have realities in the past and nothing and nobody can ever remove these assets from the past. But today's society is characterized by achievement orientation.

author: Chris Voss with Tahl Raz
quote: Think about things that are not important for you but that are important for them (or vice versa) and consider involve them in the negotiation.
refresher: Two sides may value the same terms differently. Look for something inexpensive for you and valuable to them, then exchange it for a concession with the opposite pattern.

links.title: Harvard Program on Negotiation · Logrolling in negotiation

author: Richard C. Schwartz
concept: Symptoms make more sense in context
quote: When you tell a person they are sick and ignore the larger context in which their symptoms make sense, not only do you miss leverage points that could lead to transformation, but you also produce a passive patient who feels defective.
refresher: Within the IFS model, an extreme response may have served a protective role in an earlier environment. Asking what context made it useful can reveal options that a defect label hides.

author: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer
concept: Leaders’ behavior becomes the real policy
quote: The practices modeled by the boss will be critical to guide employees as to the appropriate behavior. An office with no vacation policy but a boss who never vacations will result in as office that never vacations.

author: Brad J. Schoenfeld and Ronald L. Snarr
quote: The reality is that water requirements change based on a variety of factors including environ- ment. sweating, body surface area, calorie intake, body size. and lean muscle tissue, leading to tremendous inter- and intraindividual variation.
refresher: A single water target cannot fit every body and activity. Heat, sweating, body size, food, and exercise all change requirements, so intake should respond to conditions and individual losses.

author: Malcolm Gladwell
concept: Lower rank can make speaking up easier
quote: Planes are safer when the least experienced pilot is flying , because it means the second pilot isn't going to be afraid to speak up.

author: Christopher M. Bishop
quote: Whereas K-means algorithm performs a hard assignment of data points to clusters, in which each data point is associated uniquely with one cluster, the EM algorithm makes a soft assignment based on the posterior probabilities.

author: Jessica Fern
quote: The main difference between happy couples and unhappy couples is not that happy couples don’t have arguments or make mistakes, but that they are better and faster at doing the repair work when breaches have occurred.
refresher: Conflict and mistakes occur in every relationship. What separates resilient pairs is their ability to notice a rupture, take responsibility, and restore connection before distance hardens.

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Repair attempts in relationships

author: Charles T. Munger; edited by Peter D. Kaufman
concept: Put the reward after the necessary action
quote: You can successfully manipulate your own behavior with this rule, even if you are using as rewards items that you already possess! Granny's rule, to be specific, is the requirement that children eat their carrots before they get dessert.
refresher: The Premack principle uses a more probable or preferred activity to reinforce a less preferred one. Sequence can therefore change behavior even when the reward was already available.

author: Ray Dalio
concept: Build an organization that can work without you
quote: The greatest success you can have as the person in charge is to orchestrate others to do things well without you.
refresher: A leader’s work compounds when other people gain the authority, context, and skill to perform without constant intervention. Judge leadership partly by how well the system functions in the leader’s absence.

author: Ray Dalio
concept: Turn failures into a searchable record
quote: Issue log: tool to record mistakes and learn from them. Anything that goes wrong must be "issue logged" with the severity of the issue and who is responsible for it specified, so that it's easy to sort through most problems.
refresher: Recording an issue, its severity, and its ownership prevents mistakes from dissolving into memory. A consistent log makes recurring patterns visible and gives follow-up a clear home.

author: Walter Isaacson
concept: Cannibalize your product before a rival does
quote: One of Job's business rules was to never be afraid of cannibalizing yourself. "If you don't cannibalize yourself, someone else will".
refresher: Protecting today’s successful product can leave tomorrow’s category to someone else. A company willing to replace its own offering keeps the transition—and the learning—inside.

book: Structures: Or Why Things Don’t Fall Down
author: J. E. Gordon
quote: What is really happening in failures is that the material or the structure finds some way of evading an unduly high compressive stress, usually by moving 'out from under' the load. The actual fracture nearly always takes place by shearing.
refresher: A compressed member may fail by buckling or shearing as the structure finds a path away from the load. Analyze the movement a failure permits, not only the nominal direction of force.

author: Mark Miodownik
quote: Revolution to mass-production: rather than trying to remove the carbon until just the right amount was left, about 1 percent, Mushet suggested removing all the carbon and then adding 1 percent carbon back in.

author: Richard P. Feynman
concept: Averaging guesses cannot create missing evidence
quote: This famous problem: Nobody was permitted to see the Emperor of China and the question was, What is the length of the Emperor of China's nose? To find out, you go all over the country asking people what they think the length of the Emperor of China's nose is, and you average it.

author: Lao Tzu
concept: Desire becomes craving when it consumes attention
quote: Addiction or craving, which is what desire becomes when we allow it to absorb the finer energies of our psyche. Craving is a desire that devours us. But desires pure and simple are not to be killed or suppressed; they are an aspect of our human nature.
refresher: The commentary distinguishes ordinary desire from a demand that absorbs the mind. The useful question is not whether a desire exists, but whether it leaves room for choice and other values.

author: Timothy Ferriss
quote: Unless something is well-defined and important, no one should do it. Eliminate before you delegate. Never automate something that can be eliminated, and never delegate something that can be automated or streamlined.
refresher: Efficiency work can preserve a task that should not exist. First ask whether the activity creates enough value to keep; only then automate or delegate it.

author: Paulo Coelho
concept: Choose the story that preserves agency
quote: He has to choose between thinking of himself as the poor victim of a thief and as an adventurer in quest of his treasure.
refresher: The same loss can support two identities: passive victim or active seeker. Reframing does not erase what happened; it changes which next actions become imaginable.

author: Jonathan Haidt
concept: Less visible trouble can mask withdrawal
quote: What if teenagers are not doing as much of the bad stuff teenagers used to do not because Gen Z is getting wiser, but because they are withdrawing from the physical world?
refresher: A fall in familiar risky behavior is not automatically evidence of flourishing. Ask what replaced it: healthy engagement, or retreat from physical relationships and independent experience.

author: Erich Fromm
concept: Rational faith is confidence grounded in activity
quote: Rational faith is not primarily belief in something, but the quality of certainty and firmness which our convictions have. Faith is a character trait pervading the whole personality, rather than a specific belief. Rational faith is rooted in productive intellectual and emotional activity.
refresher: Fromm distinguishes faith as a quality of conviction from assent to a particular doctrine. In his account, it grows from productive thought, feeling, and action rather than passive acceptance.

source.file: Fromm E. - The Art of Loving_.docx

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Faith

author: Olivia Fox Cabane
concept: Mirroring must respond to emotional state
quote: Imitating someone's body language through mirroring is an easy way to establish trust and rapport. If their demeanor is angry or defensive, though, mirroring would only escalate the tension. In that case, try breaking them out of that posture.
refresher: Matching another person’s posture can signal rapport when the interaction is calm. Mirroring anger or defensiveness may amplify it, so connection sometimes requires shifting the pattern instead.

links.title: Kavanagh and Winkielman · Spontaneous mimicry and affiliation (research review)

author: Don Norman
concept: Accidents usually need several failures to align
quote: In well-designed systems, there can be many equipment failures, many errors, but they will not lead to an accident unless they all line up precisely. This is why the attempt to find "the" cause of an accident is usually doomed to fail.
refresher: Complex systems often contain multiple defenses. An accident emerges when weaknesses line up across them, so searching for one isolated cause can hide the conditions that made harm possible.

source.file: The design of everyday things notes.html

links.title: FAA · Risk Management Handbook (PDF)

author: Michael E. Gerber
concept: A business process must be repeatable
quote: The definition of a franchise is simply your unique way of doing business. And unless your unique way of doing business can be replicated every single time, you don’t own it.
refresher: A process that lives only in one person’s improvisation cannot scale reliably. Document the critical steps and expected result so another capable person can reproduce the work and improve it.

links.title: Microsoft Learn · Standardizing business processes

book: The Existential Importance of the Penis
author: Daniel N. Watter
quote: Rather than focus on universal causes for male sexual problems (i.e, performance anxiety), it is impor- tant to discover the meaning that erectile loss and erectile function have for any given man.
refresher: Watter argues against assuming one universal psychological cause for erectile difficulty. Clinical assessment should ask what function and loss mean to this person while also considering medical factors.

links.title: American Urological Association · Erectile dysfunction guideline

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Reinforcement learning searches for a policy
quote: In reinforcement learning, the machine “lives” in an environment, is capable of perceiving the state, can execute actions that bring different reward. The goal of the algorithm is to learn a policy.
refresher: An agent observes a state, takes an action, and receives a reward. Learning aims at a policy that chooses actions to improve cumulative reward, not merely a label for one input.

source.file: The hundred-page machine learning book notes.html

links.title: OpenAI Spinning Up · Key concepts in reinforcement learning

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: Manage uncertainty instead of pretending to remove it
quote: Successful investing is about managing risk, not avoiding it. Investors have never liked uncertainty, and yet it is the most fundamental and enduring condition of the investing world. It always has been, and it will always be.
refresher: Uncertainty is permanent in investing. Risk management sizes exposure, diversifies, and preserves room for error so an unfavorable outcome is survivable.

links.title: Investor.gov · Assessing investment risk

author: Eric Ries
concept: Test the assumptions carrying the most weight
quote: Basic assumptions are called leaps of faith, because the success of the entire venture rests on them. If they are true, tremendous opportunity awaits. If they are false, the startup risks total failure.
refresher: A leap-of-faith assumption is one whose failure would collapse the venture. Identify these load-bearing beliefs early and design the cheapest credible test of each one.

links.title: Strategyzer · Testing business ideas

author: Culadasa (John Yates), Matthew Immergut, and Jeremy Graves
concept: Catch distraction while it is still small
quote: Recognize when a subtle distraction has the potential to become a gross distraction before it happens. There are three kinds of subtle distractions that often becomes gross distractions: pain and physical discomfort, interesting and seemingly important insights, and emotionally charged memories or thoughts.
refresher: A distraction is easier to redirect before it captures the whole field of attention. Learn its early signals—physical discomfort, exciting ideas, or emotional memories—and return without turning the interruption into another struggle.

links.title: American Psychological Association · Mindfulness and meditation

author: Joseph Campbell with Bill Moyers
concept: Situations call different parts of character forward
quote: Our life evokes our character. You find out more about yourself as you go on. That's why it's good to be able to put yourself in situations that will evoke your higher nature rather than your lower.
refresher: Character becomes visible through action, and environments make some actions easier than others. Choose commitments and communities that repeatedly invite the qualities you want to practice.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Empirical approaches to moral character

author: Eckhart Tolle
quote: Surrender is the simple but profound wisdom of yielding to rather than opposing the flow of life. Surrender is to accept the present moment unconditionally and without reservation. It is perfectly compatible with taking action, initiation change or achieving goals.
refresher: Accepting the present means recognizing what is already true before choosing a response. It does not require liking the situation or abandoning efforts to change what happens next.

links.title: Association for Contextual Behavioral Science · Acceptance and Commitment Therapy

author: Brad Stone
concept: A user base can become political leverage
quote: Each believed that the best tactic was simply to grow, harnessing the political influence of their user base to become too big to regulate.
refresher: Rapid growth changes a regulatory contest: users become constituents who can be mobilized against restrictions. This may buy influence, but it also turns product strategy into public governance.

links.title: OECD · Digital platforms

author: Allen B. Downey
concept: Overlapping discoveries reveal a hidden population
quote: Chapter 15 (page 215): If a tester finds N bugs, and another tester finds M bugs, of which k were the same as the previous one, how many bugs are in the code? (Lincoln Index Problem) (in the exercises you also have with 3 tester)
refresher: If two independent searches find some of the same bugs, their overlap contains information about how many remain unseen. Capture–recapture methods turn that overlap into an estimate of the total population.

links.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica · Mark-and-recapture estimation

author: Daniel Kahneman
concept: Plans neglect rivals, luck, and unknowns
quote: Why are we optimistic? We anchor to our plan, neglect the skills of the others, neglect the role of luck and neglect what we don't know.
refresher: Optimistic forecasts often stay inside the plan: they picture successful execution while omitting competitors’ skill, random events, and missing information. Add those outside forces explicitly before trusting the estimate.

links.title: UK Government · Optimism bias guidance

author: Naomi Klein
quote: The beauty of these models is that when they fail, they fail on a small and manageable scale - with backup system in place. Because if there is one thing we know, it’s that the future is going to have plenty of shocks.
refresher: Systems learn more safely when experiments can fail locally and backups preserve essential functions. Keeping failures bounded turns shocks into information instead of catastrophe.

links.title: NIST · Community resilience planning

author: Harper Lee
concept: Courage can begin without hope of winning
quote: I wanted you to see what real courage is, instead of getting the idea that courage is a man with a gun in his hand. It’s when you know you’re licked before you begin but you begin anyway and you see it through no matter what. You rarely win, but sometimes you do.
refresher: Atticus defines courage as acting through a likely defeat because the attempt is still right. Success matters, but it is not the only measure of whether an action was worth taking.

links.title: Facing History & Ourselves · Moral courage

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: Statistical significance is not practical significance
quote: The result is statistically significant but not practically significant. In this case, you are confident about the magnitude of change, but that magnitude may not be sufficient to outweigh other factors such as cost. This change may not be worth launching.
refresher: A precisely measured effect may still be too small to justify cost, complexity, or risk. Evaluate the estimated magnitude and decision threshold, not only whether a p-value crosses a line.

links.title: American Statistical Association · Statement on statistical significance (PDF)

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: A rater paid by the seller has a conflict
quote: Investors remained blind to the quality of the mortgages in the securities. Their only glimpse of what lurked inside came from analyst ratings. And these analysts collected fees from the very companies whose product were rating.
refresher: When the product’s creator pays for its rating, the evaluator benefits from keeping that client. Treat the resulting score as an interested judgment and examine the underlying evidence.

links.title: U.S. SEC · Credit rating agency examinations (PDF)

author: Shunryu Suzuki
concept: Rules can create room for freedom
quote: As long as you have rules, you have a chance for freedom.
refresher: A useful constraint reduces the number of choices competing for attention. Within a stable form, effort can move from deciding what to do toward noticing how well it is being done.

links.title: Harvard Business Review · Why constraints can support innovation

author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
quote: It's better to think of distribution as something essential to the design of your product.
refresher: A product is incomplete if its intended customers cannot discover, evaluate, and adopt it economically. Choose a viable path to users while designing the offering, not after building it.

links.title: Andreessen Horowitz · Design distribution around the product and customer

author: José Saramago
concept: A familiar voice can restore identity
quote: How did they recognise each other, good heavens, by their voices, of course, it is not only the voice of blood that needs no eyes, love, which people say is blind, also has a voice of its own.
refresher: When sight and social order disappear, the characters still recognize one another through voice. The scene makes connection sensory and specific: a person can remain knowable without being visible.

links.title: Young and colleagues · Voice perception and identity recognition (research review)

book: Journey to the Centre of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
concept: Education can be treated as public infrastructure
quote: Well, sir, foreigners have their own libraries, and our first consideration is, that our humbler classes should be highly educated. Fortunately, the love of study is innate in the Icelandic people.
refresher: The passage puts broad education ahead of cultural prestige. A society’s libraries matter most when learning is available beyond its privileged classes.

source.file: Journey to the centre of the earth notes.html

links.title: UNESCO · Libraries democratize knowledge and education

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quote: The essence of love and compassion is understanding, the ability to recognise the physical, material, and psychological suffering of others, to put ourselves “inside the skin” of the other. Compassion means, literally, “to suffer with”.
refresher: Compassion requires more than a warm intention. It starts by noticing another person’s material, physical, and psychological conditions closely enough to understand what they are carrying.

links.title: Greater Good Science Center · What empathy is

author: Yuval Noah Harari
concept: Discovery begins when old maps can be wrong
quote: The first modern man was Amerigo Vespucci. He argued that the new lands discovered by Columbus were not islands off the East Asian coast, but rather an entire continent unknown to the Scriptures, classical geographers and contemporary Europeans.
refresher: Vespucci’s important move was recognizing that new observations did not fit inherited geography. Knowledge advances when contradiction is allowed to revise an authoritative map.

links.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Scientific method

author: Hermann Hesse
quote: "The reason why I do not know anything about myself, the reason why Siddhartha has remained alien an unknown to myself is due to one thing, to one single thing-I was afraid of myself, I was fleeing from myself."
refresher: Siddhartha links not knowing himself to fleeing from himself. Self-knowledge asks for contact with the experiences and motives that distraction or fear keeps outside awareness.

links.title: Association for Contextual Behavioral Science · Experiential avoidance and self-knowledge

author: Jay Sullivan
concept: Defensiveness teaches people to stop helping
quote: If when you receive feedback you become defensive or argumentative, or come up with excuses, the other people will stop giving you feedback. And when you stop receiving feedback, you stop growing. You should rather ask for feedback.
refresher: If every difficult observation meets an excuse or argument, colleagues learn that honesty is costly. Receiving feedback with curiosity keeps an information channel open even when you ultimately disagree.

links.title: Center for Creative Leadership · Feedback, trust, and defensiveness (research report, PDF)

author: Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic
concept: Graphs reveal patterns faster than tables
quote: While tables interact with our verbal system, graphs interact with our visual system, which is faster at processing information. This means that a well-designed graph will typically get the information across more quickly than a well-designed table.
refresher: Tables support exact lookup and verbal comparison. A well-designed graph uses the visual system to expose shape, direction, and outliers quickly; choose the format for the reader’s task.

links.title: Medicaid.gov · When to use a graph or a table (guide, PDF)

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Prepare capacity instead of predicting every threat
quote: Contemplating Uncertainty feels bad, because not knowing what's going to happen feels like a threat. Instead of fixating on predicting invisible and unknowable threats, it's better to channel your energy into enhancing your ability to handle the unexpected.
refresher: Uncertainty can consume attention without improving foresight. Invest instead in reserves, adaptable skills, and response options that help across many possible surprises.

links.title: Ready.gov · Business continuity and preparedness (PDF)

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: A fail-safe looks wasteful until it is needed
quote: Fail-safes are not efficient in the sense that you're investing time and resources in a system you hope you'll never use. Backup Systems and Insurance, from one perspective can be seen as a waste of money.
refresher: Backups and insurance consume resources during normal operation, which makes them easy targets for optimization. Their value appears in the rare event that would otherwise be unrecoverable.

links.title: NIST · Contingency planning guide

author: Rob Fitzpatrick
concept: Ask questions that could change the decision
quote: You can tell it's an important question when its answer could completely change (or disprove) your business.
refresher: A comfortable question may collect detail without testing the decision at stake. Prioritize questions whose answers could overturn a core belief, stop an investment, or send the plan in a different direction.

links.title: Steve Blank · Customer discovery tests the founders’ hypotheses

author: Brad J. Schoenfeld and Ronald L. Snarr
concept: Flexibility work is not a complete warm-up
quote: Flexibility exercises should not be used as the sole method of warming up. Instead, they should be performed after core temperature has been elevated to a point that the client is beginning to perspire.
refresher: Stretching alone does not prepare every system for activity. Raise body temperature first with movement appropriate to the session, then place flexibility work where it supports the task.
