links.title: Mayo Clinic · How to warm up and cool down

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: On-device models trade agility for privacy and speed
quote: The static deployment has fast execution time, preserved user privacy, and the ability to call it when offline.But it's harder to upgrade without having to upgrade the entire application and monitor performances.
refresher: Running a model on the user’s device can reduce latency, work offline, and keep data local. Updating and monitoring it becomes harder because deployment depends on the surrounding application.

links.title: Google AI Edge · LiteRT for on-device machine learning

author: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer
concept: An organization can invert the hierarchy
quote: A loosely coupled organization should resemble a tree rather than a pyramid. The boss is at the roots, holding up the trunk of senior managers who support the outer branches where decisions are made.
refresher: In the tree metaphor, leaders at the roots support the people nearest customers and decisions. Authority still exists, but its purpose is to provide context and resources outward.

links.title: Wang and colleagues · The trickle-down effects of servant leadership (research paper)

author: Christopher M. Bishop
concept: Compression can preserve everything or accept loss
quote: We can also use the result of a clustering algorithm to perform data compression. It is important to distinguish between lossless data compression (reconstruct the data exactly from the compression) and lossy data compression (we accept some reconstruction errors).
refresher: Lossless compression permits exact reconstruction. Lossy compression discards selected detail to shrink the representation further, so its usefulness depends on which errors the application can tolerate.

links.title: IBM · Lossless and lossy data compression

author: Don Norman
concept: Constraints make the valid action easier to find
quote: Constraints simplify memory. Constraint are powerful clues, limiting the set of possible actions. The thoughtful use of constraints in design lets people readily determine the proper course of action, even in novel situation.
refresher: A good constraint removes impossible or dangerous options from consideration. It guides a new user toward the right action without requiring every rule to be memorized.

source.file: The design of everyday things notes.html

links.title: Interaction Design Foundation · Constraints in design

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: Being overpriced does not make a short safe
quote: Investors believe that an overvalued stock must drop in price purely because it is overvalued, but an overvalued stock can stay overvalued for surprisingly long time. That makes short-selling too risky for mere mortals.
refresher: A valuation gap has no deadline. Short selling adds borrowing costs and potentially unbounded loss while the market can remain enthusiastic longer than the position can survive.

links.title: Investor.gov · An introduction to short sales

author: Eric Ries
concept: Efficiency cannot rescue work aimed at the wrong thing
quote: In our times, out productive capacity exceeds our ability to know what to build. What we are wasting comes not from the inefficient organization of work but rather from working on the wrong things-and on an industrial scale.
refresher: A flawless process can multiply waste when the output is unwanted. Validate that the work solves a real problem before optimizing how quickly the organization produces it.

links.title: Lean Enterprise Institute · Value and waste in lean thinking

author: Gergely Orosz
concept: Give estimates a range and assumptions
quote: You can always give an “ideal estimate,” which assumes no issues with the system. Also provide a “worst-case” estimate which assumes the system will behave strangely and that workarounds will be needed.
refresher: A single date hides uncertainty. Pair an ideal estimate with a plausible worst case and state what each assumes, so planning can respond to risk instead of mistaking precision for confidence.

links.title: Project Management Institute · Estimates should expose assumptions and uncertainty

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: Test the experiment system with identical variants
quote: Running A/A tests is a critical part of establishing trust in an experimentation platform. The idea is so useful because the tests fail many times in practice, which leads to re-evaluating assumptions and identifying bugs.
refresher: An A/A test sends users to nominally identical experiences. A significant difference or other failed invariant exposes assignment, logging, or analysis problems before they corrupt a real decision.

source.file: Kohavi R. - Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments.docx

links.title: Microsoft Research · Patterns of trustworthy experimentation before launch

author: Jordan Ellenberg
concept: Improbability is relative to a model
quote: Improbability, is a relative notion, not an absolute one; when we say an outcome is improbable, we are always saying that is improbable under some set of hypothesis we've made about the underlying mechanism of the world.
refresher: An outcome is surprising only against assumptions about how it was generated. State the model before treating a small probability as evidence; under another mechanism, the same event may be ordinary.

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: A budget makes cost overruns visible
quote: Budgeting is the act of estimating future costs and taking steps to ensure that these estimates aren't exceeded without good reason. Budgets are very important in con- trolling Profit Margins, the Cash Flow Cycle, and Leverage.
refresher: Estimate costs before committing resources, then investigate meaningful deviations. A budget is useful as a feedback boundary, not as proof that every forecast will be exact.

links.title: U.S. Small Business Administration · Manage business finances

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Delegate the purpose, not only the task
quote: Commander's Intent is a much better method of delegating tasks: whenever you assign a task to someone, tell them why it must be done. The more your agent understands the purpose behind your actions, the better they'll be able to respond appropriately when the situation changes.
refresher: When people understand why an outcome matters, they can adapt the method as circumstances change. A task without intent leaves every surprise waiting for another instruction.

links.title: U.S. Army · Understanding mission command

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Value capture must leave value for both sides
quote: Value Capture is tricky. In order to be successful, you need to capture enough value to make your investment of time and energy worthwhile, but not so much that there's no reason for your customers to do business with you.
refresher: A business must retain enough value to sustain its work while leaving customers a compelling reason to transact. Extract too little and the business fails; extract too much and demand disappears.

links.title: Strategyzer · The Value Proposition Canvas

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: Your Reputation is not directly under your control - it's the sum total of what others think about everything you do. The marketplace is the final arbiter of your Reputation, and it's always watching what you do.
refresher: You control actions, not the conclusion other people draw from them. Reputation forms across repeated experiences, so one promotional claim cannot substitute for consistent conduct.

links.title: Markkula Center · A framework for ethical decision making

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Compare an intervention with doing nothing
quote: The best way to correct for Intervention Bias is to examine what scientists call a "null hypothesis": examining what would happen if vou did nothing or assumed the situation was an accident or error.
refresher: Before crediting an action for what followed, ask what likely would have happened without it. The null alternative protects against mistaking ordinary variation or recovery for an intervention’s effect.

concept: Treat one promotion cycle as part of a long career

quote: Clarify 3, 6, and 12-month expectations with your manager, and also ideally with your skip-level manager (the manager of your manager). What are the team’s top priorities and the biggest problems to address?

author: Gergely Orosz
concept: A good career path depends on the person
quote: Career paths are diverse, and there’s no simple way to define what a “good” career path looks like, as this varies from person to person. The best you can do is figure out which career path is interesting and achievable for you.
refresher: Career quality is not a single ladder. Choose among management, technical depth, contracting, or other paths by matching the work to your interests, constraints, and attainable opportunities.

links.title: Center for Creative Leadership · Create a leadership development plan

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: Investigate surprising data before celebrating it
quote: Twyman's law, perhaps the most important single law in the whole of data analysis: “The more unusual or interesting the data, the more likely they are to have been the result of an error of one kind or another”
refresher: An extraordinary pattern may be a discovery, but it is also where logging, instrumentation, and analysis errors become most visible. Verify the data-generating path before explaining the result.

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: Balance local improvements with a few large bets
quote: In general, we recommend always having a portfolio of ideas: most should be investments in attempting to optimize “near” the current location, but a few radical ideas should be tried to see whether those jumps lead to a bigger hill.
refresher: A portfolio can fund many changes near the current product while reserving some capacity for ideas that move to a different opportunity. Local optimization alone may miss a much higher peak.

source.file: Kohavi R. - Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments.docx

links.title: Harvard Business Review · Manage an innovation portfolio

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: A goal metric should represent ultimate success
quote: Goal metrics are usually a single or a very small set of metrics that best captures the ultimate success you are striving towards. These metrics may not be easy to move in the short term.
refresher: Choose a small set of measures that express the outcome the product ultimately seeks. They may move slowly, so shorter-term diagnostic metrics can explain movement without replacing the real goal.

source.file: Kohavi R. - Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments.docx

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: Segment on attributes measured before treatment
quote: Ideally, segmenting should be done only by values that are determined prior to the experiment, so that the Treatment could not cause users to change segments, though in practice restricting segments this way may be hard for some use cases.
refresher: If treatment can change who enters a segment, comparing that segment after the experiment can introduce selection bias. Prefer categories fixed before assignment when interpreting heterogeneous effects.

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: Random assignment balances hidden causes in expectation
quote: Controlled experiments are the gold standard for assessing causality because, with random assignment of units to variants, the first term is the observed difference between Treatment and Control and the second term has an expected value of zero
refresher: Randomization makes treatment assignment independent of preexisting differences on average. That is why a treatment-control difference can support a causal claim when the experiment is implemented correctly.

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
concept: A metric denominator should include affected users
quote: The next critical question is to determine which users to consider in the denominator of the revenue-per-user metric: Only users who start the purchase process. This is the best choice, given where the change is in the funnel. We include all potentially affected users. but no unaffected users (users who never start checking out) who dilute our results.
refresher: Include everyone who could be changed by the treatment and exclude people who could not encounter it. A denominator that is too broad dilutes the signal; one chosen after treatment can bias it.

author: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, and Ya Xu
quote: When experiment results are surprising, a good rule of thumb is to replicate them. Rerun the experiment with a different set of users or with an orthogonal re-randomization.
refresher: Rerun an unexpected result with fresh users or a new randomization. Replication helps distinguish a stable effect from chance, a transient condition, or a defect in the experiment.

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: Put concurrency policy in one place
quote: Solve the problem by changing the server, which additionally changes the client: server-based locking - Better performances, reduces possibility of error, enforces a single policy because is in only one place and reduces the scope of the shared variables.
refresher: Server-side locking can enforce one synchronization rule for every caller. Centralizing the policy reduces the chance that one client forgets to lock or unlock shared state.

links.title: SEI CERT · Concurrency coding practices

author: Robert C. Martin
quote: Conundrum: all developers know messes slow them down, and yet all developers feel the pressure to make messes in order to meet deadlines. The only way to meet deadlines is to keep the code as clean as possible at all times.
refresher: Shortcuts create code that takes longer to understand and change, so deadline pressure can compound into slower delivery. Maintaining clarity keeps future work from paying interest on today’s haste.

links.title: Martin Fowler · Is high quality software worth the cost?

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: Delay irreversible choices until evidence improves
quote: We all know it is best to give responsibilities to the most qualified person. We often forget that it is also best to postpone decisions until the last possible moment. It lets us make informed choices with the best possible information.
refresher: Keeping an option open can produce a better-informed decision when more facts will arrive. The useful deadline is the last responsible moment, before delay itself removes options.

links.title: Martin Fowler · YAGNI

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: Working code still needs an editing pass
quote: The most important way to be expressive is to try. All too often we get our code working and then move on to the next problem without giving sufficient thought to making that code easy for the next person to read. Remember, the most likely person to read the code will be you.
refresher: After behavior works, spend attention on the next reader: names, structure, and intent. The next reader is often your future self, returning after the context has faded.

links.title: Google · Code review standard

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: Use a learning test to understand a dependency
quote: Instead of experimenting in our production code, we could write some test to explore our understanding of the third-party code: learning test.
refresher: Write a small test around an unfamiliar library to record what you believe it does. The test turns exploration into executable knowledge and warns when an upgrade changes relied-on behavior.

links.title: Martin Fowler · Testing dependencies and their contracts

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: Executable detail cannot be abstracted away entirely
quote: We will never get rid of code, because code represents the details of the requirements. At some level those details cannot be ignored or abstracted; they have to be specified. And specifying requirements in such detail that a machine can execute them is programming. Such a specification is code.
refresher: Requirements eventually need enough precision for a machine to execute them. Higher-level descriptions help people reason, but implementation must still resolve every behavior the system needs.

links.title: MIT Press · Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs

author: Robert C. Martin
concept: A domain language makes intent visible
quote: Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) are separate, small scripting languages or APIs in standard languages that permit code to be written so that it reads like a structured form of prose that a domain expert might write.
refresher: A small language or carefully shaped API can express rules in terms a domain expert recognizes. The design is successful when business meaning is visible without exposing incidental machinery.

links.title: Martin Fowler · Domain-specific languages

author: Osvaldo Martin
concept: A model should omit irrelevant detail
quote: Models are simplified descriptions of a given system or process that, for some reason, we are interested in. Those descriptions are deliberately designed to capture only the most relevant aspects of the system and not to explain every minor detail. This is one reason a more complex model is not always a better one.
refresher: Models are purposeful simplifications. Adding complexity helps only when the extra structure captures something relevant to the question; otherwise it can obscure reasoning and fit noise.

source.file: Martin O. - Bayesian Analysis with Python.docx

links.title: George Box · Science and statistics (paper)

author: Osvaldo Martin
quote: It is possible to create hierarchical models with as many levels as we want. But unless the problem necessitates additional structure, adding more levels than required does not enhance the quality of our model or inferences.
refresher: A probabilistic model can contain many nested levels, but each level adds assumptions and parameters. Include hierarchy when the data-generating process calls for partial pooling or grouped variation.

source.file: Martin O. - Bayesian Analysis with Python.docx

concept: Log space turns fragile products into stable sums
quote: In computational statistics, we usually perform computations in log space. This helps provide numerical stability and computational efficiency, among other things. See, for example, the preceding code block; you can see that we calculated a difference (instead of a division) and then we took the exponential before returning the result.
refresher: Very small probabilities can underflow when multiplied. Taking logarithms converts products and ratios into sums and differences, allowing the computation to preserve values that ordinary floating point would lose.

author: Osvaldo Martin
concept: Partial pooling shrinks noisy group estimates
quote: The most relevant part of this plot is that the estimates from the hierarchical model are pulled toward the partially pooled mean, or equivalently they are shrunken in comparison to the unpooled estimates.
refresher: A hierarchical model pulls group estimates toward a shared mean, with weaker groups moving more. This trades some independence for lower variance while retaining real differences supported by data.

author: Osvaldo Martin
quote: Mixture models naturally arise when the overall population is a combination of distinct sub-populations. A familiar example is the distribution of heights in a given adult human population, which can be described as a mixture of female and male sub-populations.
refresher: One aggregate distribution may combine groups with different centers or shapes. A mixture model represents those latent components and the probability that each observation belongs to them.

author: Osvaldo Martin
concept: Individual effect curves can reveal hidden variation
quote: Individual Conditional Expectation (ICE) plots are closely related to PDPs. The differ- ence is that instead of plotting the target covariates' average partial effect on the predicted response, we plot n conditional expectation curves at given fixed values.
refresher: A partial-dependence plot averages a feature’s modeled effect across observations. Individual conditional-expectation curves show each observation separately, revealing patterns that the average can conceal.

author: Benjamin Graham
quote: Being intelligent investor means being patient, disciplined, and eager to learn; you must also be able to harness your emotions and think for yourself. It’s a trait more of the character than of the brain.
refresher: Successful investing depends less on raw intellect than on patience, independent judgment, and control over reactions. A clever analysis is fragile if fear or excitement determines the action.

links.title: Investor.gov · Assessing risk tolerance

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: A falling price is not itself a reason to sell
quote: The intelligent investor never dumps a stock purely because its share price has fallen; she always asks first whether the value of the company’s underlying business has changed.
refresher: Ask whether the underlying business and original investment case changed. Selling solely because the quoted price fell lets market movement replace analysis.

links.title: FINRA · Avoid emotional investing

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: Price volatility differs from permanent loss
quote: Investors does not lose money merely because the market price of his holdings declines; hence the fact that a decline may occur does not mean that he is running a true risk of loss.
refresher: A lower market quote changes what a holding could be sold for today. Permanent loss depends on impaired value or a forced sale, so volatility and risk overlap without being identical.

links.title: Investor.gov · Understanding risk

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: A simple allocation can be good without being optimal
quote: 50-50 bond-stocks makes good sense for the defensive investor. It is extremely simple; it aims in the right direction. It may not turn out to be the best in terms of results achieved.
refresher: A balanced stock-and-bond policy may never be the best performer in hindsight. Its value comes from being understandable, diversified, and easier to follow through changing markets.

links.title: Investor.gov · Asset allocation and rebalancing

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: Rebalance by policy instead of market mood
quote: Once you set these target percentages, change them only as your life circumstances change. Do not buy more stocks because the stock market has gone up; do not sell them because it has gone down. Replace guesswork with discipline.
refresher: Set an asset allocation that fits your circumstances, then restore it deliberately when holdings drift. Changing the target because prices rose or fell turns a policy into performance chasing.

links.title: FINRA · Rebalancing your portfolio

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: An investment edge must be sound and unpopular
quote: To enjoy a reasonable chance for continued better than average results, the investor must follow policies which are inherently sound and promising and not popular on Wall Street.
refresher: A policy cannot deliver above-average results merely because it is fashionable; popularity is usually reflected in price. Any durable edge needs a valid basis that other market participants have not already adopted.

links.title: FINRA · Active and passive investing

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: A good company can still have a bad price
quote: At some point in its life, almost every stock is a bargain. Although there are good and bad companies, there is no such thing as a good stock; there are only good stock prices, which come and go.
refresher: Investment quality depends on what the buyer receives relative to what they pay. Admiring a business does not establish that its current shares offer an adequate return or margin of safety.

links.title: FINRA · Evaluating stocks

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: Frequent trading creates a reliable cost
quote: Holding stocks for a few hours at a time is financial suicide. Some of your trades might make money, most of your trades will lose money, but your broker will always make money.
refresher: Individual trades may win or lose, but spreads, fees, taxes, and attention recur with turnover. A strategy must overcome those certain frictions before activity adds value.

links.title: SEC · Investor bulletin on trading costs

author: Benjamin Graham
concept: Consensus can erase an investment advantage
quote: If all analysts were agreed that one particular stock was better than all the rest, that issue would quickly advance to a price which would offset all of its previous advantages (“efficient market hypothesis").
refresher: When nearly every analyst agrees that an asset is superior, buyers can bid that belief into the price. A correct popular story may offer little advantage after the market has already paid for it.

links.title: FINRA · Active and passive investing

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Content similarity can create a filter bubble
quote: Content-based filtering: learning what user like based on the properties of the content they consume. Problem is filter bubble, suggesting only content that looks similar to what user already consumed.
refresher: Recommending only items like those already consumed narrows what the system can reveal. A useful recommender balances relevance with diversity, novelty, and opportunities to discover new interests.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Active learning spends labels where they help most
quote: Active learning consists of start learning with relatively few labeled examples, and a large number of unlabelled ones, and then label only those examples that contribute the most to the model quality.
refresher: Begin with a small labeled set, train a model, and request labels for examples expected to improve it most. This can reduce annotation work when labels are expensive.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: One-versus-rest turns multiclass into binary tasks
quote: If you have multiclass problem but a binary classification algorithm you should use one versus rest: transform a multiclass problem into C binary classification problems and build C binary classifiers, then pick the prediction that is the most certain.
refresher: Train one binary classifier for each class against all others, then choose the strongest response. This lets a binary learning method address a problem with many labels.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Unsupervised learning finds structure without labels
quote: In unsupervised learning, the data is a collection of unlabelled examples. The goal is to create a model that solve practical problems like clustering, dimensionality reduction or outlier detection.
refresher: With no target label, a model can still group similar examples, compress dimensions, or flag unusual observations. The useful objective must come from the problem rather than a supplied answer column.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Feature scaling changes the geometry of learning
quote: Normalization is the process of converting an actual range of values which a numerical feature can take into a standard range of values (typically [-1, 1] or [0, 1]). This can increase the speed of learning.
refresher: Mapping numerical features to comparable ranges prevents one unit scale from dominating distances or gradients. Scaling often improves optimization without adding information to the data.

quote: t-SNE and UMAP are designed specifically for visualisation purposes. They uses a similarity metric between two examples to create fuzzy sets and then, with gradient descent try to minimise the change in fuzzy sets in lower space (p.119).
refresher: Methods such as t-SNE and UMAP place similar high-dimensional observations near one another in a low-dimensional view. The picture helps exploration, but its global distances and cluster shapes need cautious interpretation.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Feature engineering translates a domain into data
quote: The problem of transforming raw data into a dataset is called feature engineering. Everything measurable can be used as a feature, demands from the data analyst a lot of creativity and domain knowledge.
refresher: A learning algorithm only sees the variables supplied to it. Turning raw events into useful features requires domain knowledge about what can be measured and which representation exposes the signal.

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: Genetic Algorithms (GA) are a numerical optimisation technique used to optimise undifferentiable optimisation function. They use concepts from evolutionary biology to search for a global optimum of an optimisation problem by mimicking evolutionary biological processes (using concepts as “selection”, “crossover”, and “mutation”).
refresher: Selection, crossover, and mutation explore candidate solutions when an objective is discontinuous or not differentiable. They trade exact guarantees for a broad, population-based search.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Machine-learning progress slows as errors get harder
quote: The progress of a machine learning project is nonlinear. The error usually decreases fast in the beginning, but then the progress slows down. Because of this, it's better to make sure that the client understands the constraints and the risks. Carefully log every activity and track the time it took. This will help not only in reporting but also in estimating complexity for similar projects in the future.
refresher: Early improvements often arrive quickly, followed by diminishing gains. Track experiments and time so stakeholders can see the curve and future projects can use evidence instead of optimistic memory.

links.title: Google for Developers · Rules of machine learning

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Spot-check several algorithms before tuning deeply
quote: If you don't want to guess the best algorithm for your problem, a recommended approach is to spot-check several algorithms, and then test them on the validation set as hyperparameter.
refresher: A quick comparison across plausible model families gives evidence about which assumptions fit the data. Select promising candidates with validation results before spending heavily on one algorithm.

links.title: scikit-learn · Choosing the right estimator

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Test feature extraction as production code
quote: Feature extraction code in one of the most important parts of a machine learning system. It must be extensively and systematically tested.
refresher: Features define what the model actually receives. Unit and integration checks should catch changed units, missing values, leakage, and training-serving differences before they become silent model errors.

links.title: Google · ML test score for production systems (paper)

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: A bandit can shift traffic while learning
quote: Multi-armed bandit is another popular technique of online model evaluation. We start by randomly exposing all models to the users. Then we gradually reduce the exposure of the least-performing models until only one, the best performing model, gets served most of the time.
refresher: Start by exposing users to several models, then allocate more traffic to better-performing options while retaining enough exploration to learn. Evaluation and deployment happen together.

links.title: Microsoft Research · Multi-armed bandits

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Use machine learning when rules cannot stay explicit
quote: You should consider using machine learning to solve a business problem when the problem is too complex for coding, the problem is constantly changing, it is a perceptive problem, it is an unstudied phenomenon, the problem has simple objective, and it is cost-effective.
refresher: Machine learning earns its complexity when the task is perceptual, changing, or too intricate for maintained rules and when success has a measurable objective. A solvable rule-based task may not need it.

links.title: Google for Developers · Problem framing for machine learning

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: A representative sample can replace the full dataset
quote: When you work with big data, it's not always practical and necessary to work with the entire data asset. Instead, draw a smaller sample of data that contains enough information for learning. Different data sampling strategies can be used for that, in particular simple random sampling, systematic sampling, stratified sampling, and cluster sampling.
refresher: Working with every record may be unnecessary or impractical. Choose a sampling design that preserves the variation relevant to learning, especially for rare or structured subgroups.

links.title: NIST · Random sampling

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: Data can be stored in different data formats and on several data storage levels. Data versioning is a critical element in supervised learning when the labeling is done by multiple labelers.
refresher: A trained model cannot be reproduced from code alone. Record the exact dataset, labels, transformations, and schema used for each run so changes can be traced and compared.

links.title: Google Cloud · Data and model lineage for machine learning

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Model failure can originate anywhere in the pipeline
quote: Poor performance can be caused by a bug in your code, training data errors, learning algorithm issues, or pipeline design. In addition, learning can be sensitive to small changes in hyperparameters and dataset makeup.
refresher: Poor metrics may come from code, labels, data composition, algorithm choice, or deployment plumbing. Diagnose the pipeline layer by layer before assuming the model family is at fault.

links.title: Google for Developers · Debugging machine learning models

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: Opacity can hide risk behind mathematical authority
quote: The risk ratings on the securities were designed to be opaque and mathematically intimidating, in part so that buyers wouldn't perceive the true level of risk associated with the contracts they owned.
refresher: A complicated score can discourage buyers or citizens from asking what it measures. Mathematical presentation does not replace disclosure of inputs, assumptions, uncertainty, and incentives.

links.title: NIST · Four principles of explainable artificial intelligence

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: A screening model may optimize rejection rather than fit
quote: "The primary purpose of the [personality] test, is not to find the best employee. It's to exclude as many people as possible as cheaply as possible."
refresher: High-volume hiring tools can be designed to remove candidates cheaply instead of finding the best one. Evaluate the objective the system actually optimizes and the qualified people it excludes.

links.title: U.S. EEOC · Assessing adverse impact in software and algorithms

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: High-impact models need transparency and audits
quote: Many of these models will arrive with the best intentions. But they must also deliver transparency, disclosing the input data they're using as well as the results of their targeting. And they must be open to audits.
refresher: Good intentions do not reveal whether a model harms people. Document its input data and outcomes, permit independent scrutiny, and test performance across the groups affected by it.

links.title: NIST · AI Risk Management Framework

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: A proxy can create the outcome it predicts
quote: The practice of using credit scores in hirings and promotions creates a dangerous poverty cycle. After all, if you can't get a job because of your credit record, that record will likely to get worse, making it even harder to land work.
refresher: Using credit history to deny employment can make income and repayment harder, worsening the score used for the next decision. A model becomes destructive when its decisions feed its own proxy.

links.title: Federal Trade Commission · Employment background checks and credit reports

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: A measured outcome can be gamed at the deadline
quote: The number of "graduates employed nine months after graduation" can be gamed too. Students could also be barista. Hiring their own graduate for hourly temp jobs just as the crucial nine-month period approached.
refresher: When rank or funding depends on one reported number, organizations can optimize the reporting window instead of the underlying goal. Inspect how the metric could improve while reality does not.

links.title: Manheim and Garrabrant · Goodhart’s law (paper)

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: What a ranking omits can dominate its result
quote: The proxies the journalists chose for educational excellence make sense, after all. Their spectacular failure comes, instead, from what they chose not to count: tuition and fees.
refresher: Reasonable proxies still produce a distorted ranking when a major cost or outcome is absent. Audit a score by listing what matters to the decision and checking which parts never enter the model.

links.title: OECD · Handbook on constructing composite indicators

author: Christopher M. Bishop
concept: One-class models learn the boundary of normal data
quote: There are also single-class support vector machines, which solve an unsupervised learning problem related to probability density estimation. Instead of modelling the density of data, however, these methods aim to find a smooth boundary enclosing a region of high density.
refresher: A one-class support vector machine encloses a high-density region without needing examples of every abnormal class. Observations outside the learned boundary can be flagged as novel.

concept: EM alternates two simpler estimation steps
quote: EM algorithms breaks down the potentially difficult problem of maximising the likelihood function in two stages the E step and the M step, each of which will often prove simpler to implement.

quote: Because each step minimizes the loss, convergence is assured. However, it could converge to a local minimum rather than global minimum.

author: Christopher M. Bishop
concept: A probabilistic graph makes dependencies visible
quote: A graph comprises nodes (also called vertices) connected by links (also known as edges or arcs). Each node represents a random variable (or group of random variables), and the link express probabilistic relationship between these variables.
refresher: Nodes represent random variables and edges encode their conditional relationships. The graph exposes factorization assumptions that would be difficult to see in a single joint formula.

author: Christopher M. Bishop
concept: Logistic regression is a classifier despite its name
quote: Logistic regression is a model for classification rather than regression. Maximum likelihood can exhibit severe over-fitting for datasets that are linearly separable, that could be solved by adding regularisation term.
refresher: Logistic regression models class probability through a linear score. On separable data, unregularized maximum likelihood can push coefficients without bound, so a penalty stabilizes the solution.

author: Christopher M. Bishop
concept: Segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions
quote: The goal of segmentation is to partition an image into regions each of which has a reasonably homogeneous visual appearance or which corresponds to objects or part of objects.
refresher: Image segmentation assigns pixels to visually coherent regions or objects. It changes the task from labeling a whole image to identifying where distinct structures appear inside it.

concept: Pause before treating someone as an obstacle
quote: Prima di sbuffare perché qualcuno è lento, prima di parlare male di qualcuno appena esce, prima di trattare aualcunc come funzione, fermati e chiediti: come vorrei essere trattata io se fossi al suo posto?
refresher: A delay can make another person seem like an obstacle. Pause to consider their position, then choose a response that preserves their dignity while addressing the problem.

source.file: Giappone E. - Le Crepe Sono Fatte Per L_Oro.docx

links.title: WHO · Practising kindness and acting on values

book: Le crepe sono fatte per l’oro
author: Elena Giappone
concept: Put effort where you can act
quote: Accetto quello che non posso fisicamente cambiare. E uso mia energia mentale per gestire cosa posso cambiare.
refresher: Acceptance distinguishes a circumstance you cannot change from the next action you can take. Acknowledging a disruption can free attention for practical choices without requiring you to like what happened.

source.file: Giappone E. - Le Crepe Sono Fatte Per L_Oro.docx

links.title: WHO · Practical skills for coping with stress

author: Gergely Orosz
quote: The test of readable code is simple: can others understand it?
refresher: Familiarity can hide confusing code from its author. Ask a reviewer to follow the logic; unclear names, unnecessary complexity, and missing context become easier to see through another reader.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Google Engineering Practices · Reviewing complexity, names, and comments

author: Gergely Orosz
quote: Practice refactoring as often as possible. Getting good at refactoring is similar to learning to code. You can read all you like about a topic, but without doing it you’ll never truly master it.
refresher: Build refactoring skill through small changes that preserve behavior. Keep tests close and inspect the result after each step, so improving structure becomes a regular part of development.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Martin Fowler · Refactoring as behavior-preserving change

author: Gergely Orosz
concept: Give each pull request one purpose
quote: Break your changes into one small PR each, with each PR changing one thing only.
refresher: A focused change gives reviewers a clear question to answer. Separate unrelated work so the intent, tests, and possible rollback remain understandable without reconstructing several changes at once.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Google Engineering Practices · Why small changes are easier to review

author: Gergely Orosz
concept: Make code review helpful and humane
quote: Better code reviews are also empathetic. They recognize that the person who wrote the code spent a lot of time and effort on the change. These code reviews applaud nice solutions and are generally positive in tone.
refresher: Critique the change with specific reasons and recognize what works well. Respectful review can improve the code while making it easier for its author to learn and ask questions.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Google Engineering Practices · Writing courteous, useful review comments

author: Brad J. Schoenfeld and Ronald L. Snarr
quote: Proper equipment selection is essential for creating an optimal resistance training program. Variables such as a client's training status, personal preference, familiarity, balance, coordination, strength, and knowledge of proper exercise technique should be taken into consideration.
refresher: Equipment choice depends on the person and the movement. Match the tool to their experience, coordination, and goals instead of assuming one type of equipment suits everyone.

source.file: Schoenfeld B. J. - NSCA’s Essentials of Personal Training.docx

links.title: ACE · Free weights versus strength-training equipment (PDF)

author: Brad J. Schoenfeld and Ronald L. Snarr
quote: Free-weight equipment allow unrestricted movement in all planes of motion, rather than a largely fixed movement path
refresher: Free weights allow a less constrained path than many machines. That freedom also asks the lifter to control and stabilize the movement; it is a trade-off to consider alongside the training goal.

source.file: Schoenfeld B. J. - NSCA’s Essentials of Personal Training.docx

links.title: HPRC · Comparing strength-training options

author: Brad J. Schoenfeld and Ronald L. Snarr
concept: Teach the setup before the repetition
quote: Demonstration of a new exercise given to a client should begin with how to establish a starting position.
refresher: Instruction starts before the weight moves. Establish the starting position and equipment adjustments first, then demonstrate the movement; a chest-press seat adjustment is one concrete example.

source.file: Schoenfeld B. J. - NSCA’s Essentials of Personal Training.docx

links.title: NASM · Chest-press machine setup and technique

author: Bill Perkins
concept: Experiences can pay a memory dividend
quote: Unlike material possessions, which seem exciting at the beginning but then often depreciate quickly, experiences actually gain in value over time: They pay what I call a memory dividend.
refresher: Perkins calls the later enjoyment of an experience a memory dividend. Recalling or sharing a meaningful event can extend its value beyond the moment it happened.

links.title: Cornell · How sharing experiences contributes to happiness

author: Bill Perkins
concept: Count the time behind earned money
quote: So any amount of money you've earned through your work represents the amount of life energy you spent earning that money.
refresher: Perkins frames earned money as time and effort already spent. Consider that cost when deciding what to buy or how much extra work to take on; time itself can be part of the payoff.

links.title: Whillans and colleagues · Buying time promotes happiness (research paper)

author: Bill Perkins
concept: Balance future security with present enjoyment
quote: So, yes, the grasshopper would be better off to save a little and, yes, the ant would be better off to live a little!
refresher: The ant and grasshopper illustrate competing priorities: preparing for later and living now. Perkins argues for deliberate balance. Enjoyment belongs in a plan alongside obligations, resilience to shocks, and future needs.

links.title: CFPB · Financial well-being includes security and freedom of choice

author: Jessica Fern
refresher: Anxiety concerns whether others will be available; avoidance concerns discomfort with dependence and closeness. Use these dimensions to notice patterns, rather than treating a style as an unchangeable identity.
quote: Some researchers have proposed that attachment is better described using the two dimensions of attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance, and looking at the different ways these dimensions can interact.

links.title: Chris Fraley · Adult attachment theory and research

author: Jessica Fern
refresher: A boundary can preserve closeness while making room for personal needs. Name what you are comfortable with and listen to the other person’s limits; connection need not require abandoning yourself.
quote: Porous boundaries arise when we are connected but not protected, and rigid boundaries stem from being protected, but not connected. Healthy boundaries are when we are connected and protected.

links.title: love is respect · Understanding personal boundaries

author: Jessica Fern
refresher: The defining condition is mutual knowledge and consent. Discuss what each person agrees to, rather than assuming that a shared relationship label means identical expectations.
quote: Consensual nonmonogamy is an umbrella term for the practice of simultaneously having multiple sexual or romantic partners where everyone involved is aware of and consents to the relationship structure.

links.title: Division 44 CNM Committee · What consensual nonmonogamy means

author: Jessica Fern
refresher: Fern distinguishes having a relationship from choosing to be attachment figures. Clarify whether each person wants to offer dependable comfort and support for exploration, instead of assuming that commitment means the same thing to everyone.
quote: The antecedent to being polysecure with your partners is first getting clear about whether you want to be attachment figures for each other.

links.title: Chris Fraley · Safe havens and secure bases in adult attachment

author: Jessica Fern
refresher: Reserve a mutually workable time for attention without competing screens. Presence becomes something partners can count on, rather than something squeezed between notifications.
quote: It can be helpful to have designated times of the day or during the week where you are both off your phone and focused on each other, so that the times when you are on your phone throughout the day do not become problematic.

links.title: Gottman Institute · Creating rituals of connection

author: Jessica Fern
concept: Express what makes a partner precious
refresher: Name a specific act of care and why it mattered. Expressed appreciation makes affection visible instead of asking a partner to infer it from the relationship’s existence.
quote: With your partners, take on a gratitude practice where you set aside a regular time to each appreciate the ways in which they’ve been supportive or shown up that have been meaningful to each of you.

links.title: Gottman Institute · Shared meaning and appreciation rituals

author: Jessica Fern
refresher: Try to understand your partner’s experience before fixing or evaluating it. Paraphrase what you heard and ask whether you understood, leaving room for correction.
quote: Attunement is meeting your partner with curiosity, wanting to understand their feelings and needs. It is the feeling of being seen, understood and “gotten” by the other.

links.title: Greater Good in Action · Active listening

author: Jessica Fern
refresher: In Fern’s framework, recurring moments together help make care predictable. Agree on a greeting, check-in, or shared activity that fits this particular relationship rather than copying someone else’s routine.
quote: Our attachment system is comforted by routine and regularity.

links.title: Gottman Institute · Examining relationship rituals

author: Jessica Fern
concept: Offer yourself the care you offer a friend
refresher: Secure relating also includes how you respond to yourself. Acknowledge a difficult moment with kindness while still taking responsibility for what needs to change.
quote: I am talking about the importance of positive self-talk and being kind and loving to yourself in ways that you would probably treat a friend, but so frequently forget when it comes to your relationship with yourself.

links.title: Kristin Neff · The elements of self-compassion

author: Michael E. Gerber
concept: Work on the business that serves your life
refresher: Step back from delivery to design how the business should operate. Judge that design against the life you want it to support, including your time and responsibilities.
quote: Once you recognize that the purpose of your life is not to serve your business, but that the primary purpose of your business is to serve your life, you can then go to work on your business, rather than in it, with a full understanding of why it is absolutely necessary for you to do so.

links.title: SBA · Planning a business

author: Michael E. Gerber
concept: Document the routine before handing it over
refresher: A process that lives only in someone’s memory makes each handoff an exception. Write down the steps, expected result, and points requiring judgment so another person can perform and improve it.
quote: Without documentation, all routinized work turns into exceptions.

links.title: GitLab · Using and maintaining a shared handbook

author: Michael E. Gerber
concept: Measure whether an innovation actually helps
refresher: Choose an outcome before changing the process. Compare results with the prior approach, then keep, adjust, or discard the change instead of equating novelty with improvement.
quote: To be at all effective, all Innovations need to be quantified. Without Quantification, how would you know whether the Innovation worked? By Quantification, I'm talking about the numbers related to the impact an Innovation makes.

links.title: ASQ · Plan, do, check, act

author: Michael E. Gerber
concept: Give each responsibility a clear owner
refresher: List the work and expected outcomes before assigning people. One person can hold several roles, but each responsibility needs a clear owner and an understood handoff.
quote: If everybody's doing everything, then who's accountable for anything?

links.title: Atlassian · Defining roles and responsibilities

author: Culadasa (John Yates), Matthew Immergut, and Jeremy Graves
refresher: The book distinguishes the object in focus from the wider field you can still notice. During practice, attend to the breath while allowing surrounding sensations to remain present.
quote: Conscious experience takes two different forms, attention and peripheral awareness. Whenever we focus our attention on something, it dominates our conscious experience. At the same time, however, we can be more generally aware of things in the background. Those are two ways of "knowing" the world. In meditation, we work with both attention and peripheral awareness to cultivate stable attention and mindfulness.

links.title: Greater Good · Mindfulness and awareness

author: Culadasa (John Yates), Matthew Immergut, and Jeremy Graves
concept: Reward noticing that the mind wandered
refresher: Noticing distraction is part of the practice. Recognize that moment without self-criticism, then gently return to the chosen object.
quote: A critical moment occurs during mind-wandering when you suddenly realize you're no longer observing the breath. Loosing your focus wan't something you did, it happens unconsciously. And how do you train something that happens unconsciously? Simply take a moment to enjoy and appreciate "waking up" from mind-wandering. Avoid becoming annoyed or self-critical about mind-wandering. You should positively reinforce introspective awareness.

links.title: Greater Good in Action · Returning to the breath

author: Culadasa (John Yates), Matthew Immergut, and Jeremy Graves
concept: Notice an emotion without becoming its label
refresher: Describe impatience as a present experience rather than your identity. This shift can create room to observe the feeling and choose how to respond.
quote: Impatience is an emotion. Act as you should act with all the emotions while meditating. Don't identify with it by thinking 'I am impatient'. Regard it as just one more feeling that arises and passes away, thinking 'Impatience is arising'.

links.title: Greater Good in Action · Noticing thoughts and feelings

author: Culadasa (John Yates), Matthew Immergut, and Jeremy Graves
concept: Allow background thoughts without chasing them
refresher: The aim here is not an empty mind. Let a passing thought remain in the background while returning attention to the practice, without fighting it or following its story.
quote: You aren't trying to eliminate the distractions entirely from awareness. As long as they stay in the background, let them come, let them be, and let them go.

links.title: Greater Good in Action · Mindful breathing

author: Culadasa (John Yates), Matthew Immergut, and Jeremy Graves
concept: Use walking as an attention practice
refresher: Walking offers a different anchor from seated breath practice. Notice the changing sensations of contact and movement; when attention drifts, return to those sensations.
quote: When you catch your mind wandering, simply bring yourself back to the present by focusing your attention on the sensations in your feet.

links.title: Greater Good in Action · Walking meditation

author: Daniel Kahneman
quote: Make a list of factual questions to assess the reliability of the trait and think how to score the answers.
refresher: Choose job-relevant criteria and score comparable evidence for each candidate. Consistent questions and rating standards reduce the room for a memorable impression to dominate the hiring decision.

links.title: U.S. OPM · Structured interviews

author: Daniel Kahneman
concept: Expert intuition needs a learnable environment
quote: Intuition in experts is nothing more than recognition.
refresher: A confident hunch is more trustworthy when the setting contains stable patterns and repeated practice brings useful feedback. Experience in an unpredictable setting can build confidence without building reliable expertise.

links.title: Gary Klein · When to consult your intuition

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Validate demand with a manual service
quote: I headed down to the local shoe store, took pictures of their stock, and put them on the Website. Every time someone bought something on the site, I’d buy it from the store and ship it to them. For a big believer in technology, I couldn’t have found a more primitive way to do it.
refresher: The first version can test whether customers will actually buy before expensive infrastructure exists. Manual fulfillment is useful evidence gathering; it still needs honest promises and workable unit economics.

links.title: Paul Graham · Do things that do not scale

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Separate a good decision from a lucky result
quote: One of the most interesting things about playing poker was learning the discipline of not confusing the right decision with the individual outcome of any single hand.
refresher: Evaluate the information, alternatives and risks available when the choice was made. One lucky win can hide a poor process, while one unlucky loss need not invalidate a sound decision.

links.title: Baron and Hershey · Outcome bias in decision evaluation

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Optimize the customer relationship beyond one sale
quote: [Call centric suggesting competitor’s website cause they are out of stock] We’re not trying to maximise each and every transaction. Instead, we’re trying to build a lifelong relationship with each customer, one phone call at a time.
refresher: Helping a customer find a suitable alternative can sacrifice today’s transaction while earning future trust. Judge service by lasting usefulness and repeat relationships, not only immediate revenue or call speed.

links.title: Jeff Bezos · Long-term customer focus in the 1997 shareholder letter

author: Tony Hsieh
concept: Design work around progress and connection
quote: Happiness is really just about four things: perceived control, perceived progress, connectedness (number and depth of your relationships), and vision/meaning (being part of something bigger than yourself).
refresher: Hsieh offers a practical happiness framework, not an exhaustive formula. Give people meaningful choices, visible progress, supportive relationships and a purpose they can understand; related motivation research emphasizes autonomy, competence and relatedness.

links.title: Center for Self-Determination Theory · Autonomy, competence and relatedness

author: Brad Stone
concept: Early growth may require work that cannot scale
quote: “Paul was the first person to give us permission to say, It’s okay to think about things that may not scale, to break away from the mythology of Silicon Valley. We could actually think creatively around how to grow the business."
refresher: Airbnb’s founders improved individual listings and met hosts themselves. Such work can reveal the obstacles automation would otherwise reproduce; scale the solution after learning what customers actually need.

links.title: Paul Graham · Recruiting and helping early users manually

author: Brad Stone
concept: A marketplace must build both sides together
quote: The relatively few listings on the site drew few guests looking for travel accommodations, and the paucity of guests didn’t inspire potential new hosts to embrace the unorthodox concept of making their homes available to total strangers over the internet.
refresher: Guests need useful listings, while hosts need evidence of demand. Concentrating early effort in a narrow market can create enough successful matches for each side to make joining worthwhile.

links.title: Paul Graham · Airbnb and the difficulty of starting marketplaces

author: Mike Michalowicz
quote: Sales - Profit = Expenses
refresher: The formula changes the budgeting order, not accounting arithmetic. Reserve a deliberate profit amount, then design operations around the remaining cash while meeting existing obligations.

links.title: FDIC · Managing cash flow

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Give each dollar a separate purpose
quote: Each of these accounts has a differ ent objective: one is for profit, one for owner compensation, another for taxes and another for operating expenses.
refresher: The small-plates system separates cash for profit, owner pay, taxes, and operating costs. The operating balance becomes a spending boundary; the total bank balance is not all available to spend.

links.title: FDIC · Cash planning and allocation

author: Mike Michalowicz
quote: Move your PROFIT account and other "tempting" accounts out of arm's reach.
refresher: Separate reserves from everyday spending so an impulsive decision requires an extra step. Keep necessary access for genuine obligations; friction is a behavioral aid, not a substitute for cash planning.

links.title: CFPB · Where to keep dedicated savings

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Give cash allocation a recurring rhythm
quote: Enforce a Rhythm: Do your allocations and payables twice a month (specifically, on the tenth and twenty-fifth). Don't pay only when there is money piled up in the account.
refresher: A fixed review schedule makes allocation a routine instead of a response to a large balance. The book chooses twice monthly; coordinate the actual schedule with payroll, bills, and tax deadlines.

links.title: BDC · Budget and monitor cash flow

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Move from current allocations toward targets
quote: TAPs are not your starting point; TAPs are the targets you are moving toward. (Take them from the following table)
refresher: First measure where cash actually goes. Adjust allocations gradually and review affordability instead of immediately imposing the book’s target percentages on a business with different obligations.

links.title: FDIC · Planning realistic cash flows

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Separate owner labor from ownership returns
quote: Don't confuse the profit distribution with Owner's Comp, which is pay for working in the business. Profit is a reward for owning the business.
refresher: Owner compensation recognizes work performed; profit distributions recognize ownership. Keeping them distinct exposes a business that appears profitable only because its owner works unpaid. Actual payment and tax treatment depend on the business structure.

links.title: IRS · Compensation and distributions

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Reserve tax money before it becomes a surprise
quote: So don't steal from your TAX account, thinking you won't need that money for taxes.
refresher: Tax reserves are earmarked obligations, not spare operating cash. Estimate them from the business’s actual tax position and payment dates; a generic percentage in a book cannot determine the amount owed.

links.title: IRS · Estimating and paying taxes

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Retain a buffer instead of distributing everything
quote: As your profits accumulate in your PROFIT account, and you only take 50 percent as a profit distribution, the remainder will act as a rainy-day fund.
refresher: The book’s half-distribution rule deliberately leaves a reserve. The transferable principle is to keep liquidity for interruptions; the appropriate buffer depends on costs, volatility, and access to funding.

links.title: BDC · Reserves for seasonal cash flow

author: Mike Michalowicz
concept: Do not budget from your best month
quote: The trap we fall into is believing our most recent best month is our new normal. Then we start running the business according to that "normal.”
refresher: Separate a temporary sales spike from sustainable earning capacity. Compare similar seasons and use rolling history plus a forward cash forecast before taking on recurring costs.

links.title: BDC · Build and update a cash forecast

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: The five connected parts of a business
quote: Every successful business (1) creates or provides something of value that (2) other people want or need (3) at a price they're willing to pay, in a way that (4) satisfies the purchaser's needs and expectations and 5) provides the business sufficient revenue to make it worthwhile for the owners to continue operation.
refresher: Trace value creation, marketing, sales, delivery, and finance. A brilliant product still needs reachable buyers, completed purchases, reliable delivery, and sustainable economics. Diagnose the missing connection before optimizing one department.

links.title: Strategyzer · Map a complete business model

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Test the assumptions that could kill the business
quote: Critical Assumptions are facts or characteristics that must be true in the real world for your business or offering to be successful.
refresher: List what must be true about demand, delivery, and willingness to pay. Test the assumption whose failure would invalidate the offer before committing heavily to building it.

links.title: Eric Ries · Validated learning and minimum viable products

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: A minimum viable offer tests a purchase
quote: A Minimum Viable Offer is an offer that promises and/or provides the smallest number of benefits necessary to produce an actual sale. A Minimum Viable Offer is essentially a Prototype that's been developed to the point that someone will actually pull out their wallet and commit to making a purchase.
refresher: Reduce an offer to the smallest useful promise a customer will actually buy. Compliments and signups are weaker evidence than a genuine purchasing decision; be explicit about what is available and when.

links.title: Eric Ries · Validated learning and minimum viable products

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: Attempting to appeal to everyone is a waste of time and money: focus your marketing efforts on your Probable Purchaser.
refresher: Name the customer whose problem your offer solves particularly well, where they look for help, and what they value. Relevance to that group matters more than attention from everyone.

links.title: SBA · Market research and business planning

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: It's often far more comfortable to focus on the features: you know what your offer does. Even so, it's far more effective to focus on the benefits: what vour offer will provide to customers.
refresher: A feature describes the product; a benefit explains its effect on the buyer. Connect each important capability to a concrete customer problem and the result it helps achieve.

links.title: SBA · Market research and business planning

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: Your Next Best Alternative is what you'll do in the event you can't find Common Ground with the party you're negotiating with.
refresher: Compare a proposed agreement with what you can realistically do without it. Improve that alternative and compare terms on the same basis, including time, risk, and switching costs.

links.title: Harvard Program on Negotiation · Evaluate your BATNA

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: A Value Stream is the set of all steps and all processes from the start of your Value Creation process all the way through the delivery of the end result to your customer.
refresher: Follow an order from the first input to the customer receiving value. Make waiting, handoffs, and rework visible; speeding up one local step may leave total delivery time unchanged.

links.title: Lean Enterprise Institute · Value-stream mapping

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: A balance sheet is a snapshot
quote: A Balance Sheet is a snapshot of what a business owns and what it owes at a particular moment in time.
refresher: Assets show what the business controls; liabilities show its obligations; equity is the residual. Read successive snapshots alongside income and cash-flow statements to see how the financial position changes.

links.title: SEC · Reading financial statements

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Recognized revenue is not collected cash
quote: In accrual accounting, revenue is recog nized immediately when a sale is made (i.e. a product is purchased, a service is rendered etc.), and the expenses associated with that sale are incurred in the same time period.
refresher: Revenue recognition follows the applicable earning or delivery rules, not simply cash receipt or signing a sale. A sale can appear in income before payment arrives, so monitor collections and payment timing alongside profitability.

links.title: SEC · Reading financial statements

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: Lifetime Value is the total value of a customer's business over the lifetime of their relationship with your company. The more a customer purchases from you and the longer they stay with you, the more valuable that customer is to your business.
refresher: Estimate repeat purchases and retention, then account for delivery costs and the time needed to recover acquisition spending. An optimistic lifetime-revenue forecast does not justify unlimited marketing expense.

links.title: Shopify · Acquisition models and lifetime value

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Every choice has an opportunity cost
quote: Opportunity Cost is the value you're giving up by making a Decision.
refresher: Compare your decision with the best realistic alternative you must give up. Time and attention count even when no money changes hands; an affordable project can still crowd out a better one.

links.title: Federal Reserve Education · Opportunity cost

author: Josh Kaufman
concept: Improve the constraint before the rest
quote: The performance of a System is always limited by the availability of a critical input. Alleviate the Constraint, and the system's performance will improve.
refresher: Find the bottleneck that limits the whole process. Protect its capacity from avoidable interruptions, improve it, then look again: the limiting step may move elsewhere.

links.title: Lean Enterprise Institute · Theory of constraints

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: Measurements that don't help you make improvements to your System are worse than worthless: they're a waste of your limited Attention and energy.
refresher: Choose measures tied to customer outcomes and the system’s purpose. For each dashboard number, name the decision it could change; easy-to-count activity can conceal disappointing results.

links.title: Rob Ewaschuk · Monitoring useful signals

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: Here's the Paradox of Automation: the more efficient the Automated system, the more crucial the contribution of the human operators of that system. When an error happens, operators need to identify and fix the situation quickly or shut the system down - otherwise, the Automated system will continue to Multiply the error.
refresher: As routine work disappears, people may lose the practice needed during exceptions. Keep failures visible and rehearse recovery so the human fallback remains capable when automation stops behaving as expected.

links.title: Lisanne Bainbridge · Ironies of automation

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Keep final evaluation separate from tuning
quote: Parameters of the model are optimized by the learning algorithm based on training data. The values of hyperparameters are tuned by using the validation dataset. The test set is only used to assess the model's performance and report it to the client or product owner.
refresher: Repeatedly choosing models against the test set turns it into training feedback. Tune with validation data or cross-validation, then use the untouched test set to estimate generalization.

links.title: scikit-learn · Cross-validation and held-out evaluation

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Split raw data before learning preprocessing
quote: Split was applied to raw data
refresher: Imputation, scaling and feature selection can leak information even before model training. Fit these transformations only on each training partition, then apply the fitted transformation to held-out examples.

links.title: scikit-learn · Preventing preprocessing leakage

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: Errors made by a machine learning model can be uniform and appear in all use cases with the same rate, or focused and appear in just certain types of use cases. Focused errors are those merit special attention, because fixing an error pattern, you fix it once for many examples.
refresher: Inspect concrete failures and group them by cause. A missing feature or systematic labeling mistake can affect many examples; addressing that shared cause is often more valuable than another broad tuning sweep.

links.title: Martin Zinkevich · Rules of machine learning and feature iteration

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Limit exposure while testing a deployment
quote: Canary deployment: pushing the new version to a small fraction of the users, while keeping the old version running for most users. Allows model performance validation and won't affect too many users in case of possible bugs.
refresher: Release to a small representative slice, monitor predefined quality and reliability signals, and retain a rollback path. A canary reduces the blast radius; it does not prove safety for every user group.

links.title: Google SRE · Canarying releases

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: The models deployed in production must be constantly monitored. The goals are to make sure that the model is served correctly, and that the performance of the model remains within acceptable limits.
refresher: A model can keep answering while its usefulness deteriorates. Track prediction quality, input distributions and operational health, with alerts tied to meaningful thresholds and someone responsible for responding.

links.title: Martin Zinkevich · Monitoring training-serving skew

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Predictions can change the next training dataset
quote: An effective runtime is secure and correct, ensures ease of deployment and recovery, provides guarantees of model validity, and avoids training/serving skew and hidden feedback loops.
refresher: Recommendations influence what people see and click. Treat those observations as consequences of a policy, not an unbiased picture of preference; otherwise retraining can amplify the model’s own earlier choices.

links.title: Martin Zinkevich · Avoiding feedback loops with positional features

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: If the model predicts well training data but predicts poorly the validation/test set, we say that the model has high variance or that the model overfits
refresher: When training errors are small but held-out errors are large, the model may be fitting noise or dataset-specific details. Compare both curves before deciding whether to simplify, regularize or collect more representative data.

source.file: The hundred-page machine learning book notes.html

links.title: Google · Overfitting and regularization

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: Regularization force the algorithm to build a less complex model (slight increase of bias, big decrease of variance).
refresher: Regularization trades some training fit for a model that may generalize better. Tune its strength against held-out performance: too much can erase real signal, while too little can preserve accidental patterns.

source.file: The hundred-page machine learning book notes.html

links.title: Google · L2 regularization and model complexity

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Precision and recall answer different questions
quote: Precision is the ratio of correct positive predictions to the overall number of positive predictions.
refresher: Precision asks how many positive predictions were correct; recall asks how many actual positives were found. Choose a threshold according to the consequences of false alarms and missed cases, not accuracy alone.

source.file: The hundred-page machine learning book notes.html

links.title: scikit-learn · Precision-recall curves

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: Cross-validation: you split your training set into several (typically, five) subsets of the same size (folds). You use the examples in all but one set as training set and the leftover as validation set. You repeat this for all the sets and use the average result as final value.
refresher: Each fold gets a turn as unseen evaluation data. Average the scores to compare candidate settings, while preserving a final test set and using grouped or time-aware splits when observations are dependent.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Gradient descent improves parameters step by step
quote: Gradient descent is an iterative optimisation algorithm for finding the minimum of a function. Starts at some random point and takes steps proportional to the negative of the gradient of the function at the current point.
refresher: The gradient points toward increasing loss, so an update moves the opposite way. The learning rate controls the step size; useful progress depends on both the objective and a suitable update scale.

author: Andriy Burkov
quote: Random Forest is bagging algorithm where a certain number of “copies” are sampled with replacement from the training set and then train decision trees with those (reducing the variance of the final model). At each split of the decision tree, a random subset of the features are inspected.
refresher: Averaging many trees helps most when their errors are not identical. Bootstrap samples and random feature subsets diversify the trees, reducing variance relative to one highly flexible tree.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Boosting adds models to correct remaining errors
quote: Boosting consists of using the original training data and iteratively creating multiple models by using a weak learner that try to “fix” the errors which previous model made (example: Gradient Boosting).
refresher: Boosting builds an ensemble sequentially, directing new learners toward what the current ensemble misses. Learning rate, depth and number of rounds control how aggressively it fits the training data.

author: Andriy Burkov
concept: Transfer learned representations to a new task
quote: In transfer learning, you pick an existing model train on some dataset, and you adapt this model to predict examples from another dataset.
refresher: Reuse features learned on a related dataset, then train a new output head or carefully fine-tune the network. Check domain fit and held-out performance rather than assuming pretrained knowledge always transfers.
